description:
fix: surface real pip error when plugin install fails (#1409) (#1479)

When both OSS and PyPI installs failed, pipInstall returned a generic 'both OSS and PyPI unavailable' message that masked the real pip stderr (e.g. a forbidden --user install inside a virtualenv), so users could not diagnose the root cause. Capture the OSS and PyPI pip stderr separately and include them in the returned error via a new pipErrorDetail helper. Applied to both appmanagerutil and computenestutil, which share the same install logic, plus hermetic regression tests.

description:
• Fixed an issue where hosting:clone failed to locate source sites in other projects. (#11247)
  • Updated Pub/Sub emulator to version 0.8.37.
  • Fixed an issue where analytics timeouts could mask command errors or cause successful commands to exit with an error. (#6989)
  • Fixed an issue where unhandled exceptions during Cloud Functions deployment could be silently ignored and exit with code 0 (#6989).
  • Added crashlytics:heapdumps:{enable,disable,status} commands to manage Crashlytics Android heap dump collection. (#11225)
  • Removed unused dependencies proxy-agent, universal-analytics, and @apphosting/common.
  • Fixed an issue where throttled task queues stopped processing remaining tasks when a task exhausted its retries or timed out (#6989, #11040).
  • Fixed a race condition in SourceTokenScraper that could cause concurrent function deployments to hang when refreshing an expired source token (#6989).
  • Fixed an issue where a Function Kit and a functions codebase sharing the same source directory failed firebase.json validation. (#11253)
  • Fixed an issue where Cloud Functions creation did not retry on HTTP 403 service account propagation errors. (#11251)
  • Updated Auth deployment to use existing apps from any platform before creating a default web app. (#11250)
  • No longer grant unecessary TRUNCATE privilege to writer roles in dataconnect:sql:migrate. (#11276)
  • Updated the Firebase SQL Connect local toolkit to v3.4.23, which includes the following changes:
    • Updated the Golang dependency version to 1.26.9.
    • Improved Native SQL query validation, wrapper aliasing, and line-comment handling to support the SQL editor in Firebase SQL.

description:
Support Firebase SDK auto-initialization for Cloud Run services (#11208)

* Use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call when checking autoinitVars keys

* Ensure runtime service account has roles/firebase.sdkAdminServiceAgent for SDK autoinit

* Use ternary instead of numeric length in object spreads

* Add defensive optional chaining in run.ts and runv2.ts

* Remove unused Deployable predeploy/postdeploy from RunSingle

* Create a basic, initial schema for firebase.json

* improve testing

* Require region, remove serviceAccount, and register run in Config.KNOWN_PROPS

* Remove unused Deployable predeploy/postdeploy from RunSingle

* Update shared GCP clients (runv2, run, artifactregistry)

* Add direct_cloud_run experiment flag

* Add defensive optional chaining in run.ts and runv2.ts

* Rename direct_cloud_run experiment to directcloudrun

* Add firebase init run interactive setup

* Use directcloudrun experiment and validate rootDir is a directory

* Trim baseImage input in init run

* Add firebase deploy --only run for remote Cloud Build source deploys

* Clean up temporary source archive, guard release URI, and use directcloudrun

* Avoid empty template.annotations when deploy message is unset

* Simplify template.annotations cleanup when deploy message is unset

* Add firebase run:services:update command

* Validate service region and check all matching configs in updateService

* Rename masterTimeout option to pollTimeoutMs in runv2

* Use pollTimeoutMs option when creating and updating Cloud Run services

* Make updateMask fallback in updateService more readable

* Add comment explaining default updateMask calculation in updateService

* Type Service.ingress as IngressTraffic union in runv2

* Format updateMask call with Prettier and guard template literal in runv2

* Fix Policy stub type in prepare.spec.ts

* Improve readability of firebase init run and remove mainContainer

* Remove sidecar container from deploy.spec.ts

* Use dirExistsSync from fsutils in init run promptRootDir

* Make Cloud Run temp-file cleanup best-effort

A failure to delete the temporary source archive is now logged at debug level instead of thrown, so it can't fail a deploy that succeeded or replace the real upload error. Mirrors the cleanup in deploy/apphosting/deploy.ts.

* Make local build scratch dir cleanup best-effort

Route both scratch dir deletions through removeTempPath so a cleanup failure can't fail a successful deploy or replace the real deploy/build error.

* Fail clearly when SDK autoinit can't be set up, and simplify it

- A Firebase Web App that can't be looked up now fails the deploy whether it's newly or already linked, instead of deploying without autoinit. The error includes the cause and how to switch or unlink the app.
- Split resolveAutoInitEnv into flat, single-purpose helpers and use getError for the original error.
- run:services:update --app no longer rebuilds when the service already uses that app.
- Suggest asking an admin when granting the Admin SDK role fails.
- Document that FIREBASE_CONFIG is the Admin SDK's runtime config and why prepare resolves it.

* Always refresh FIREBASE_CONFIG from the linked app

Deploy writes FIREBASE_CONFIG onto the container, and the next deploy treated any value on the container as a user override. So the CLI's own first value won forever: linking an app and later enabling Storage never gave the service a storageBucket. While an app is linked, deploy now always writes the app's current config, replacing whatever is on the container, including secret-backed values. Build-time overrides still go through the build env annotation.

* Always rebuild in run:services:update, even if nothing changes

Clearing a base image that isn't set no longer skips the deploy. run:services:update always rebuilds and deploys, the same as firebase deploy, instead of trying to detect no-op updates.

* Always rebuild for --app and --clear-app too

run:services:update no longer skips the deploy when the app is already linked or there's no app to clear, so every setting behaves the same. Clearing the app now only removes FIREBASE_CONFIG from a service that was linked, since the CLI set it there; on a service that was never linked, it's the user's own value.

* Don't default to a base image in init run

A base image turns on automatic base image updates, which are off by default. So init no longer suggests nodejs22. An existing service still defaults to its own base image.

* Add firebase init run interactive setup

* Use directcloudrun experiment and validate rootDir is a directory

* Trim baseImage input in init run

* Improve readability of firebase init run and remove mainContainer

* Use dirExistsSync from fsutils in init run promptRootDir

* Don't default to a base image in init run

A base image turns on automatic base image updates, which are off by default. So init no longer suggests nodejs22. An existing service still defaults to its own base image.

* Make upsertRunConfig easier to read

Spell out what init changes on an existing service (rootDir and region) instead of merging three spreads. upsertRunConfig now adds the default ignore list itself, so actuate no longer passes it. Behavior is unchanged; added a test for the ignore fallback on existing services.

* Make upsertRunConfig easier to read

Spell out what init changes on an existing service (rootDir and region) instead of merging three spreads. upsertRunConfig now adds the default ignore list itself, so actuate no longer passes it. Behavior is unchanged; added a test for the ignore fallback on existing services.

* Don't add an ignore list to an existing service in init run

Re-running init on a service that's already in firebase.json filled in the default ignore list when the entry didn't have one. Init doesn't ask about ignore, so it shouldn't change it: an existing entry now only gets the rootDir and region the user just chose. New services still get the default ignore list.

* Default init run's root directory to the saved one, matching by service ID and region

Pressing Enter now keeps the root directory saved in firebase.json instead of resetting it to /. Cloud Run service IDs are only unique within a region, so entries now match on both; the same ID in another region gets its own entry.

* Default init run's build location to the saved localBuild setting

Pressing Enter no longer switches a service that builds locally back to remote builds.

* Only deploy the service init set up, not same-ID services in other regions

Init deploys with --only run:, which matches that ID in every region. Init now also passes the service's region to deploy, which skips services in other regions. firebase deploy and --only run: are unchanged.

* Write firebase.json once, from init, instead of also from init run's actuate

Init already writes firebase.json after every feature is set up, so the write in actuate only printed "Wrote configuration info to firebase.json" a second time. Leaving the write to init also means a failed init leaves firebase.json untouched.

* Remove the Cloud Run deploy E2E suite

scripts/run-deploy-tests ran the real CLI against a real project. Nothing ran it automatically (npm test only covers src/, and CI doesn't list it), and each run left Cloud Build images behind in Artifact Registry. The unit tests cover the logic, and live testing is done by hand.

* Let --only run:: pick one Cloud Run service

Service IDs are only unique within a region, so firebase.json can list the
same ID in more than one region.

- run: still deploys that ID in every region it's listed in, and
  now logs which services it matched when there's more than one.
- run:: deploys exactly one service. Init deploys the
  service it set up this way, which replaces the region it used to pass in
  the deploy context.
- Per-service messages (uploading, building, deployed) include the region.
- firebase.json can't list the same service ID and region twice.

* Make run:services:update change exactly one service

firebase run:services:update  now also accepts
:.

- If firebase.json lists the service ID once, the region is optional.
- If it lists the ID in more than one region, the command fails and lists
  the : names to choose from.
- It deploys only run::, so it never redeploys the same
  ID in another region.

The "doesn't exist yet" message also suggests the command that deploys
just that service and region.

* Make the Cloud Run deploy code and tests easier to read

- deploy.ts reads as four steps: upload the source, build it, prepare
  the revision, then create the service or roll out a new revision. The
  revision rules are a pure function, revisionTemplate, with one small
  test per rule.
- Helpers that only deploy.ts uses (deployRevision, toAppHostingConfig,
  the rollout timeout) moved there from util.ts. util.ts now only picks
  services from firebase.json and checks whether a service exists.
- Stop deleting the local source zip. It's a tmp file, which firebase
  deploy deletes when it exits; App Hosting relies on the same thing.
- Check every service's region once, up front, and stop --only
  filtering at the first service that isn't in firebase.json.
- Tests use realistic names, check only the fields they're about, and
  drop duplicate coverage. The release test has its own file.
- The help text no longer mentions local builds or run:services:update,
  which later PRs add.
- Clearer docstrings and tests for init run's actuate and
  upsertRunConfig.

* Make run:services:update easier to read

- Read the flags into a settings object and pass it straight to deploy.
- Move the missing-service message into update.ts, its only caller.
- Tests: realistic names, an update() helper that reads like the CLI call,
  one expectDeployed() helper, and one test for the always-rebuild decision.

* Move build env to its own PR

Build-time env vars and secrets (the buildConfig.environmentVariablesAndSecrets
annotation) move to bapi_build_env, so this PR only adds local builds.

* Make local builds easier to read

- deploy() creates the scratch folder and deletes it in one finally.
- Explain the App Hosting Backend that the Node.js version check needs.
- Init's base image validation is one expression.

* Keep localBuild's options on one line

* Support build-time env vars and secrets for Cloud Run

Reads the firebase.google.com/buildConfig.environmentVariablesAndSecrets
annotation on the service. Plain values go to Cloud Build and local builds;
secret references only work in local builds, which read them with the
deployer's credentials.

* Make the build env tests easier to read

Realistic names (API_URL, NPM_TOKEN, npm-token) and shorter fixtures.

* Make the local build tests easier to read

- deploy: split the end-to-end local build test, stub the scratch folder
  instead of touching the filesystem, and keep #11205's upload stub.
- prepare: drop a test of an implementation detail.
- init: answer prompts with one helper, one behavior per test, and split
  the upsertRunConfig localBuild test into on and off.

* Make the SDK auto-init tests easier to read

- Realistic app IDs, small fixture helpers, and no prettier-mangled calls.
- Drop two tests that repeated others, and test that prepare rejects a
  service it can't build before looking up the app or touching IAM.

* Address review comments on the Cloud Run deploy

- Add mainContainer() so one place decides which container is the main one.
- Resolve the sticky base image with an if statement instead of a ternary.
- Build the buildpack request with an explicit if instead of a conditional
  spread.
- Explain that svc.baseImage is already resolved by prepare.
- Rename createService to createNewService.

* Split run:services:update's service name into serviceId and region

updateService took one name that was either  or :. It now takes serviceId and region, and the command takes the region from --region.

* Say which deploy step sets each ServiceDeploy field

* Split Cloud Run deploys into remote and local build paths

deploy() now calls deployRemoteBuild or deployLocalBuild. Each path has its own upload function, and local builds get their own revision template, so there are no more RevisionCode unions or repeated localBuild ternaries. The local build's output is passed between functions instead of being stored on ServiceDeploy. The local build guard's fix now uses run:services:update's --region flag.

* Let a local build's env vars replace the service's values

The env vars a build reports describe that build's output, like its start command, so they now replace any env var of the same name on the service instead of being skipped. The service's other env vars are kept.

* Use App Hosting's secret format for build secrets

A build secret is now written the way apphosting.yaml writes one ({"secret": "npm-token@3"}) and passed straight to loadSecret, so there are no extra regexes or format conversions. Cloud Build gets an explicit filter for plain values instead of a cast, and the comments and errors say why only local builds can use secrets.

* Rename plainValues to nonSecretValues

The name and doc comment now say that the result never includes secrets or their values.

* Accept numbers and booleans in the build env annotation, like apphosting.yaml

* Check for secrets with isSecretRef instead of typeof string

* Make the FIREBASE_CONFIG and annotation logic in deploy easier to follow

Name the case where a deploy unlinks the app. Keep an emptied env list instead of deleting it: to Cloud Run, [] and no env field mean the same thing. Always send the service's annotations, instead of only when the linked app changed, which removes the undefined return and the conditional update mask.

* Rename serviceAnnotations to serviceAnnotationsToDeploy

* Fail the deploy if the linked Firebase Web App doesn't exist

For an app ID with no app, the web app config lookup returns the project's config without an appId, so a typo in --app deployed and was saved on the service. Check that the app exists first, with the same check App Hosting's --app uses, so the deploy fails before building or saving anything.

* Group the linked app's ID and config into ServiceDeploy.autoInit

* init run: ask which web app to link, and create a new one only in actuate

* Stop granting roles/firebase.sdkAdminServiceAgent; print the grant command when linking an app

* init run: fail instead of deploying unlinked when the web app can't be created

description:
fix(hosting): implicitly resolve site project IDs in hosting:clone (#11275)

* fix(hosting): implicitly resolve site project IDs in hosting:clone

### Description

In #11229, `hosting:clone` was updated to use project-scoped API requests and defaulted unspecified project IDs to `needProjectId(options)`. Because Firebase Hosting site IDs are globally unique, users previously cloned across projects without specifying the source project (e.g. `firebase hosting:clone site-a:live site-b:live --project=project-b`), which broke in 15.33.0 when `site-a` belonged to a different project than `--project`.

This change updates `hosting:clone` to implicitly look up the owning project for a site via `getSite("-", siteId)` when a project ID is not explicitly provided in the `[:]:` or `[:]@` argument. Once resolved, all subsequent API operations (`getChannel`, `createChannel`, `cloneVersion`, `createRelease`, `addAuthDomains`) continue to use the resolved project ID on project-scoped endpoints.

Also updates the command help text and validation error messages to document the optional `:` prefix.

Fixes #11247

### Scenarios Tested

- Unit tests in `src/commands/hosting-clone.spec.ts`:
  - Same-project channel and version cloning.
  - Explicit cross-project cloning (`::`).
  - Implicit cross-project cloning when source site is in a different project than `--project` (#11247).
  - Implicit project resolution when `--project` is omitted.
  - Error handling when a site is not found (404).

### Sample Commands

```bash
firebase hosting:clone site-a:live site-b:live --project=project-b
firebase hosting:clone site-a:live site-b:live
firebase hosting:clone project-a:site-a:live project-b:site-b:live
```

description:
refactor: Make `stacks` command use the arguments package for CLI flag and argument handling (#39338)

This change moves the `stacks` command's argument parsing logic into the `arguments` package and adds unit tests.

The `stacks` command's requirements when handling arguments are unique and are unlike conventional command implementations in the CLI.

As an example of a conventional command implementation, the `plan` command needs to define all possible flags that a user may supply to that command, and when the flags' values are parsed there will be an error raised for each unexpected flag. The positional arguments supplied to a command are basically 'anything left un-parsed after encountering the first non-flag in the slice of argument strings', which is behaviour from the `flag` package from the standard library. We need to define per-command logic to detect if there is an unexpected number of positional arguments, if they don't have the correct format, etc. Generally, commands expect to be in the form `terraform [global options]   [options specific to the command] [positional arguments]`.

The `stacks` command is unique because it forwards flags and arguments to the stacks plugin down stream. However, the `stacks` command itself takes a flag argument. The `flags` package has an all-or-nothing approach to parsing flags, which would require the `stacks` command to define all possible flags that it could be forwarding, in addition to the flag that it directly uses. This isn't maintainable, so instead we ignore all flag-parsing errors and expect the downstream plugin to raise errors. A consequence of this decision is that all flags are consumed during parsing, so we need to manually process the original slice of strings to create a new slice that has the `stacks`-specific flag removed but retains all other flags. This behaviour is characterised in unit tests in `arguments/stacks_test.go`.

Ideally, systems calling this command would be updated to use `terraform stacks -plugin-cache-dir=foobar -- arg1 arg2` instead of the current `terraform stacks -plugin-cache-dir=foobar arg1 arg2`. The double dash would allow any flags that need to be passed onto downstream systems to be avoided by parsing logic. They would be retrievable via `cmdFlags.Args()`, alongside any non-flag arguments. This would enable the logic in this change to raise errors when unexpected flags are encountered.

新增本地安全策略

新增 ve configure safety-policy，可在发送 OpenAPI 请求前拒绝指定操作，或要求人工确认。安全策略默认关闭，启用后覆盖普通 API 调用、--force 调用和 MCP call_api。

  • 规则采用 service:action 格式，支持 * 通配符、不区分大小写，按第一条匹配规则执行；未匹配的操作默认允许。服务别名、带版本号和下划线的命令共享规则。
  • 支持 deny（本地拒绝）、confirm（执行前确认）和 allow（显式允许）。add 命令只接受 deny / confirm；allow 可通过 JSON 文件或环境变量配置。
  • 提供启用、停用、查看、添加、移除和列出规则的命令。策略独立保存于 ~/.volcengine/safety-policy.json，支持环境变量覆盖。
  • 交互式终端命中 confirm 时提示确认；Agent / MCP 客户端应先向用户说明操作并取得批准，再按原参数重试。确认参数仅跳过 confirm，不能绕过 deny。
  • 校验规则格式；策略文件损坏或环境变量格式非法时返回错误，不发送 API 请求。保存策略失败时保留原文件。

配置示例：

ve configure safety-policy enable
ve configure safety-policy add --pattern '*:Delete*' --action deny
ve configure safety-policy add --pattern '*:Update*' --action confirm
ve configure safety-policy list

安全策略是客户端防护，与火山引擎 IAM 互补；ve arkcli、ve tosutil 等代理 CLI 不在拦截范围内。详见安全策略配置。

MCP 新增文档检索工具

ve mcp 的工具由 4 个扩展为 6 个，新增两项无需云凭证的公开文档能力：

  • search_docs：搜索火山引擎公开文档，可按服务代码过滤，返回标题、URL 和文本摘要。
  • fetch_docs：获取文档正文，支持按 Unicode 字符偏移分页读取。

call_api 每次调用都会重新加载本地安全策略，并在解析云凭证和发送请求前检查规则。获批重试时可传入 yes: true，该参数不能绕过拒绝规则。详见 MCP 使用文档。

升级

或通过 npm：

npm install -g @volcengine/cli@1.2.0

Add OSUtil, the database's reader of the process environment (#27199)

Split out of #26739: this adds the interface only, with two users to
show it. Moving the engine's own environment reads onto it stays in
#26739.

Extensions have no engine API to read the environment with, so they call
`getenv` directly and settings cannot apply to it. `OSUtil` is owned by
`DatabaseInstance` and reached with `OSUtil::Get(db)`.

**The API**
- `GetEnv(name, value)` reads on the user's behalf. It returns false
when the variable is unset and throws a `PermissionException` when
`enable_external_access` is disabled, the way the file system reports
refused access. A string-returning overload exists for convenience.
- `GetEnvUnrestricted(name, value)` reads configuration: the engine's
own variables (`HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `SLURM_*`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `TZ`) and
the ones the embedding application declares in
`DBConfigOptions::configuration_env`, in the `DBConfig` it hands to the
`DuckDB` constructor. `OSUtil` takes that list when the database is
configured, before anything can be loaded into it, so an extension
cannot widen the set. Any other name is an `InternalException`, so the
method cannot be used to route around the setting.
- `OSUtil::GetConfigurationEnv(name)` is static and reads only the
engine's own configuration variables, for reads that happen before a
database exists.

**Users**
- The shell's SQL `getenv()` reads through `GetEnv`.
- The aws extension reads the container credential variables through
`GetEnv`, with a patch under `.github/patches/extensions/aws` that
passes the database into its credential chain. Under
`enable_external_access=false` the `container` credential chain entry
now errors with a permission message instead of "must be set in the
environment". The patch applies on top of
`0003-credential-chain-external-access.patch` on the pinned revision,
but was not compiled locally.

**Verification**
- `test/api/test_os_util.cpp` covers allowed and refused reads,
configuration reads with and without a database, unknown names and
variables declared by the embedder.
- The `[api]` group, secrets and settings suites and the shell's
`getenv` tests pass. `make extension-patch-check` passes.

description:
ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY: check the key columns for NULLs under the append lock (#26920)

Fixes #26067.

`ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY` builds the index from a scan of the table
and checks the scanned keys and the transaction's local storage for
NULLs. A row another transaction commits after the scan is never
checked, so a NULL inserted concurrently can remain in the key column
once the ALTER commits.

**The change**
The `DataTable` that takes over the table with the new constraint holds
the parent's append lock, so no other transaction can commit rows into
the table while it is created. It already verifies a new NOT NULL
constraint over all committed rows there, but skipped UNIQUE
constraints, which is how a primary key is stored. For a primary key it
now verifies NOT NULL on the key columns.

**Verification**
- `test/sql/alter/add_pk/test_add_pk_concurrent_null.test` races `ALTER
TABLE t ADD PRIMARY KEY (id)` on a 100,000-row table against `INSERT
INTO t VALUES (NULL)` from another connection with `concurrentforeach`,
10 times with a different delay before the insert, and checks that no
NULL is left when the primary key was added. It fails in every run
without the change (10 of 10) and takes about 0.15 seconds; it requires
a vector size of at least 512.
- The `add_pk`, index, constraint, alter and transaction suites and the
`[api]` group pass.

Batch 3 of 3 of follow-ups to #8599 ([batch 1](https://github.com/netlify/cli/pull/8605), [batch 2](https://github.com/netlify/cli/pull/8626)). Out of an abundance of caution, that PR was kept purely focused on type changes.

- Share one poller between `waitForDiff` and `waitForDeploy` instead of duplicating code
- Resolve the drop deploy poll with the ready deploy
  - `waitForDropDeploy` captured the ready deploy in an outer variable and returned it with a
    non-null assertion after polling. The poll now resolves with it directly via
    `pWaitFor.resolveWith`.
- Rethrow the final drop upload error from inside the retry loop
  - The drop file upload retry loop remembered the last error, skipped the backoff on the final
    attempt, and threw the remembered error after the loop. It now throws directly on a permanent
    failure or on the last attempt, and otherwise backs off and retries. The status is read through
    an `instanceof Error` guard instead of a cast.
- Don't return the upload promise to the backoff emitter. It wasn't used, resulting in lint errors
  about promise misuse.

- Only upload in-memory bodies for static files
  - Every upload built its body with `body ?? fs.createReadStream(filepath)`, although only the

- Build the functions config with `Object.fromEntries`

    now built by a named `toFunctionConfigPayload` mapper and `Object.fromEntries`, which also gives
    the payload a derived type.

description:
docs: re-work telemetry docs

This addresses two issues:
- Netlify CLI's telemetry was under-documented
- The public facing docs were describing details only relevant to contributors

This re-works the docs to adress both of these.

feat: report CI environment CLI runs

This adds two properties to telemetry events:
- `ci_vendor`: stable identifier of CI env, e.g. `GITHUB_ACTIONS`
- `ci_is_pr`: whether the CLI is running in CI in the context of a pull/merge/etc. request
product_or_resource: feat: report CI environment CLI runs

description:
fix: send telemetry and error reports in CI environments

It was never intentional for Netlify CLI to have a blanket disable in CI environments. This was a bug, stemming from
code that intended to just disable it _when running our own tests_.

**Potentially breaking change:** If you run Netlify CLI in an environment where you block or allow-list network egress,
you may need to allow requests to `https://cli.netlify.com`. Alternatively, you can opt out of telemetry entirely by
setting `NETLIFY_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.
product_or_resource: fix: send telemetry and error reports in CI environments

description:
test: explicitly disable telemetry in our own tests

We currently disable telemetry _in CI_, including... Netlify CLI actually running in any user's CI environment.

This also implicitly disables telemetry _when running CLI's own tests in CI_.

This PR makes the latter explicit (as a precursor to removing the former behaviour).
product_or_resource: test: explicitly disable telemetry in our own tests

description:
feat: support `NETLIFY_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, `DO_NOT_TRACK` (#8620)

#### Summary

Previously, users could opt out of telemetry collection by running
`--telemetry-disable`, which wrote the configuration to a config file.

This also adds support for opting out by setting
`NETLIFY_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` or `DO_NOT_TRACK` to any value other than
`""`, `"0"`, or `"false"`.

`DO_NOT_TRACK` is an emerging standard: https://donottrack.sh/

fix: list nested subcommands in help output (#8616)

#### Summary

`netlify database --help` shows no COMMANDS section, so `database
connect` (and `database migrations apply|new|pull|reset`) can't be found
from the CLI.

The help formatter only lists subcommands named `parent:child`
(`env:get`, `sites:create`, …). The `database` commands are registered
as nested commander subcommands (`dbCommand.command('connect')`), so
their names never match the `database:` prefix and they're filtered out.

This includes a command's own nested subcommands in the list and shows
them by their full path, so each line is runnable:

```
$ netlify database --help
...
COMMANDS
  $ database connect      Connect to the database
  $ database init         Interactive setup: install the package, scaffold a
                          starter migration, and verify the database
  $ database migrations   Manage database migrations
  $ database reset        Reset the local development database, removing all
                          data and tables
  $ database status       Check the status of the database, including applied
                          and pending migrations
```

`netlify --help` and the colon-style pages (`env`, `sites`, …) render
exactly as before. Added snapshot tests for `help database` and
`database migrations --help`. Both fail without the fix.
product_or_resource: fix: list nested subcommands in help output (#8616)

ci(release): re-review repaired syncs and re-resolve them when next moves (#7205)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** Since #7124, no Claude-resolved `sync/develop-into-next` PR
has been auto-approved by `supabase-oss`. Claude's repair commit moves
the head past the only AI review, so the approval gate (review head must
equal PR head) never passes. This adds one bounded AI re-review after a
repair, and when `next` moves and conflicts at fast-forward time, Claude
re-resolves the same PR instead of asking a maintainer.

**Before**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[AI review on X] --> B[Claude repair pushes Y]
  B --> C{"review head == Y?"}
  C -- no --> D[skip forever]
  D --> E[human approves]
  F[next moved + conflict] --> G[ask human to resolve]
```

**After**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[AI review on X] --> B[Claude repair pushes Y]
  B --> C[one AI re-review on Y]
  C -- "clean or all answered" --> D[supabase-oss approves]
  C -- "needs a fix / CI red" --> E[maintainer]
  F[next moved + conflict] --> G["Claude re-resolves same PR
(max 2 resyncs)"]
  G --> A
```

### Why

On #7158, the AI review saw `39034946` and the repair pushed `b064c720`.
Every later `sync-repair` run then logged "Nothing to repair; the AI
review did not see this head." until a maintainer approved it. On #7112,
`next` moved after approval and the resync conflicted, which left the PR
waiting on a person.

### What changed

- A resolution is everything after the latest resolve comment (from the
first Claude resolve or a resync). Repair rounds count per resolution,
using release-bot comments and reviews sorted by time.
- After a repair push, `sync-repair` posts a re-review marker, and a
separate `actions: write` job dispatches the AI review once. The job
that runs Claude never gets that permission. If the dispatch fails, it
tags maintainers.
- After the re-review, rounds can only reply to findings. Claude
declines repeats by pointing at its earlier replies. If a finding needs
a fix or CI fails, the PR goes to a maintainer. Nothing is pushed in
these rounds.
- `fast-forward`: if `next` moved and merging it into an approved
`develop`→`next` sync conflicts, it dispatches `sync-branches.yml` with
a new `resync_pr` input. That re-runs the resolve, check, fix and
publish steps on the same branch and PR. The limit is 3 resolutions. A
PR resolved by hand counts as one. If the dispatch fails, or the limit
is reached, it falls back to today's "resolve by hand" message.
- `resync_pr` only accepts an open same-repository
`sync/develop-into-next` → `next` PR.
- On a `sync/develop-into-next` PR, the AI review gets
`sync-resolution.diff`: each sync merge as `--remerge-diff`, plus the
commits made on the sync branch. Both prompts and the adjudicator limit
findings to what that resolution introduced, or to code on one side that
uses something the other side removed. Previously the review re-checked
all of `develop` since the last sync, and most of its findings were
dismissed as "not from the merge".
- `release-process.md` documents the new rules.

- [x] Tests added or updated for the change.

## TL;DR
brings  `upgrade-notice` to effect & the effect lint

## whats introduced?

- the check reads files through `FileSystem`, 
the latest release through `HttpClient`, env through `Config` and the
working and home directories through `RuntimeInfo`
- `runCli`'s post-success hook now takes these services from the cli
runtime instead of providing its own

the old entry is removed, which deletes a symlink or hard link itself,
and the file is recreated exclusively with mode `0644`

stale cache file in a read-only cache directory no longer refreshes, so
each command checks the release again

ci(cli): fail mirror detection on registry errors instead of re-pushing every image (#7194)

`detect-unmirrored-images.ts` treated any failed `docker buildx
imagetools inspect` as "not mirrored" and discarded stderr. A registry
blip during detection therefore flagged every pinned image for a
re-push. In [Mirror template images run
93](https://github.com/supabase/cli/actions/runs/38847585115), all 19
images were flagged even though every one was already mirrored. The
images published to ECR Public by their own release pipelines then
failed with `403 Forbidden` on the blob HEAD.

The probe now treats only a registry `not found` as unmirrored. Any
other inspect failure aborts detection with the target and the
registry's error, so a probe failure shows up as one red detect job with
its cause instead of a fan-out of misleading push failures.

description:
chore(cli): bring `/shared` under the effect skill (#7164)

## TL;DR

most of `/shared` already followed the effect skill after its effect
lint coverage in CLI-2458,
this picks up the few things that were left

## whats introduced?

- functions deploy retries and rate limit waits move from hand written
loops to `Effect.retry` and `Effect.repeat` with a `Schedule`, keeping
the same attempts, delays and messages
- `serve` outcomes become `Data.TaggedEnum` values matched with
`$match`, and the shutdown grace uses `Effect.timeoutOrElse`
- `Predicate.isTagged` and exhaustive matching replace `_tag` checks, so
the trace sanitizer now handles every decision explicitly
- casts and non null assertions give way to narrowing, and `consent`
encodes through Effect
- the feedback client and project link state use `Effect.fn`
- tests run on `it.effect` wherever the clock does not matter, and the
malformed ref services test now asserts no request is sent

## notes

- no user facing behaviour changes at all
- the four new spans only appear in trace output and the

fix(stack): claim native backend ports across stacks until the backend stops (#7184)

Two native stacks started at the same time could end up running their
Logflare backends on the same private port. Each native backend port was
held only by a placeholder listener, and that listener closes right
before the backend is spawned. Logflare takes a few seconds to boot and
then binds with `SO_REUSEPORT`, so another stack's scan could pick the
same port in that window, and both Logflares bound it. The kernel then
split connections between the two stacks, so a request carrying one
stack's API key could reach the other stack's Logflare and get a 401.
This was the intermittent `401` from the analytics marker in the native
whole-stack lifecycle e2e.

- Native backend ports (10000–19999) are now claimed in the per-user
port registry (`ports.sqlite`). The claim is taken before the
placeholder binds and released only after the backend process stops, so
other stacks' scans skip the port for the whole handoff.
- A claim whose stack has no running owner, or whose registration is
gone, is taken over. A same-stack claim not held by the current owner
process is treated as left by a dead owner.
- A registry error fails the port scan straight away instead of being
retried as a bad port.
- `CatalogOptions.claimNativePort` is required, and the owner wires it
to the registry.

chore(cli): require every command to declare its permissions (#7185)

Closes the command permission mapping: every command leaf now declares a
permission status, so the pending list is gone.

The six commands that still hand off to the bundled Go binary (`db
branch create|delete|list|switch`, `db remote changes`, `gen keys`)
declare `unmapped` with reason `go-delegated`. The completeness test now
requires a declaration on every leaf, and a second check fails if a path
on the go-delegation allowlist stops being a real leaf declared
`unmapped`. The pending list and the registry test that depended on it
are removed; the `Undeclared` lookup result stays for command groups.

Findings: `unmapped` records how these commands are implemented, not
what they need. Reading the Go source, the four `db branch` leaves make
no Management API calls, `gen keys` makes one
(`V1GetPostgrestServiceConfig`), and `db remote changes` runs the same
diff as `db diff` against the linked database. All six could be mapped
later, which would let the `unmapped` status and its allowlist go.

Untested conditions: the six `unmapped` commands make no claim, so
nothing checks them. No blocks without a real-layer test, no best-effort
label turned required, no `OPERATIONS_WITHOUT_FGA` entries.

fix(stack): pin analytics to Logflare 1.50.15 (#7182)

Local Studio logs pages fail with "Backend error" on the default
Postgres analytics backend (#7155). Logflare 1.52.0 and later cast
endpoint query parameters such as `@project` to `jsonb` when translating
to Postgres, so every logs query fails with `invalid input syntax for
type json` (Logflare/logflare#4158).

- Pins `analytics` back to Logflare 1.50.15 (slim `v1.50.15-r1`), the
last release before the regression, in the stack catalog and both
service Dockerfiles.
- Adds an `UPGRADE_HOLDS` entry for `analytics` to the slim release
planner so the bump bot can't upgrade it again. Hotfix revisions of
1.50.15 still go through. Remove the entry once Logflare ships a fix.

The per-minute log chart still fails on the Postgres backend because
`IFNULL` is never translated (Logflare/logflare#4159); that has been the
case in every Logflare version.

A local database first created by Logflare 1.53.x (CLI 2.121.0) keeps
its Oban tables only in `_analytics`, which 1.50.15 doesn't read. On
those databases the analytics alerting and event-touch workers restart
in a loop and log `relation "public.oban_jobs" does not exist`. Log
ingestion and queries are unaffected, and `supabase stop --no-backup`
clears it.

description:
Release notes

586 merged pull requests since 2.1.0, from 31 contributors.

Important

Hoodi: Glamsterdam activates on Mon, 26 Oct 2026, 17:42:48 UTC (timestamp 1793036568, epoch 132352). Hoodi nodes must run 2.2.0 or later before then. Your consensus client must support Glamsterdam on Hoodi as well.

Note

Upgrading from 2.0.x or 1.39.x? The breaking changes below cover 2.1.0 → 2.2.0 only. Apply the 2.1.0 breaking changes first (and, from 1.39.x, the 2.0.0 breaking changes and upgrade checklist).

For most nodes this is an in-place upgrade with no resync and no config change. Read Breaking changes first if you set JsonRpc.Host / JsonRpc.EngineHost to a host name, run with Init.DiagnosticMode=VerifyTrie or FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true, use KeyStore.BlockAuthorAccount, pipeline requests over WebSocket or IPC, consume Parity-style trace_* output, or build plugins against Nethermind.

Highlights

  • Amsterdam (Glamsterdam) on Hoodi. The fork is scheduled at 1793036568 (Mon, 26 Oct 2026, 17:42:48 UTC), and Hoodi's chainspec now carries its correct beacon-chain genesis timestamp. (#14489, #13732)
  • Catch up finalized blocks from block access lists. On chains with EIP-7928, a node that is behind rebuilds the state of consensus-finalized ancestors from their verified block access lists and receipts instead of executing them, and executes only the unfinalized tail. It is on by default (Sync.ReconstructFinalizedStateFromBlockAccessLists=true). Missing data or a commitment mismatch falls back to execution. (#14157)
  • Faster tracing on Amsterdam blocks. A single-transaction trace (debug_traceTransaction, trace_transaction, trace_replayTransaction) on a block with a block access list no longer replays the transactions before the target, and whole-block traces run in parallel. All parallel block tracing now shares one node-wide budget, JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism (default 4). (#13906, #14363)
  • Blocks that load many large contracts. Glamsterdam allows 64 KiB contracts and 200M-gas blocks, so one block can touch ~58k distinct maximum-size contracts. The code DB moves from Snappy to LZ4 (mean block time on such a devnet range 2.6 s → 1.7 s, no block ≥ 6 s), missed code is copied once instead of twice (allocations per block 7.17 → 3.59 GB), and a block keeps the code it loaded for the rest of the block. (#13907, #14086, #14322)
  • Lower engine_newPayload latency. Storage trie nodes on the flat backend are written after the block is reported valid, committed storage writes are applied on an idle thread during execution, block-processing stages share one worker budget, sender recovery no longer competes with the transactions root, Kestrel reads large payload bodies in 64 KiB blocks, and the payload pipeline is warmed before RPC opens (first-payload latency 66.8 ms → 5.4 ms in the PR's measurement). (#14058, #14059, #14182, #14164, #14213, #14443, #13931, #14481)
  • Prewarmer hand-off. Block processing takes over a transaction the prewarmer already executed when its recorded footprint matches the state the block has reached, instead of executing it again (hidden Blocks.PreWarmHandoff, on by default; not used for blocks with a block access list or under EIP-8037). (#14312, #14476)
  • Parity-style trace standardisation. A long series of trace_* fixes aligns Nethermind with the draft trace spec (execution-apis#890) and with Erigon/Reth: failed precheck frames, reverted-frame results, Parity error labels, trace_filter mode/blockHash, trace_get by traceAddress path, null for unknown transactions, and stricter parameter validation. Several of these change output; see Breaking changes. (#13957, #13981, #13857, #14111, #13858, #13937)
  • Geth-compatible debug tracing. keccak256PreimageTracer, Geth opcode-logger byte limits, debug_traceCall txIndex, block-wide callTracer log indices, corrected trace-file records, and per-request V8 runtimes so JavaScript traces run in parallel. (#13662, #13670, #13700, #13693, #13709, #13727, #13737, #13541)
  • Faster JSON-RPC serialization. Blocks, RPC transactions and logs are written by source-generated writers (full eth_getBlockByNumber with 200 txs −13% time / −93% allocations; eth_getLogs of 1,000 logs −14%), and public WebSocket/IPC connections process up to 16 requests concurrently. (#14299, #14345)
  • New mainnet_aztec config with a rolling 4,096-block trace window on the flat-history backend and the per-transaction trace index. (#14038)
  • SendPolicy plugin (opt-in). Checks every transaction submitted through the node's JSON-RPC against an owner-written rule file (allowed senders/destinations, token-call allow-lists, fee and spend caps) and refuses the ones that break it. Off by default (SendPolicy.Enabled=false). (#14396)
  • Next-fork prototypes (not scheduled on any public network). EIP-8141 frame transactions with EIP-8250 keyed nonces and EIP-8272 recent roots, EIP-7979, EIP-8131, EIP-3298, EIP-7668, EIP-8253, EIP-8279. They activate only through explicit chainspec/genesis keys or the Bogota fork alias. (#12526, #13932, #13929, #13928, #13934, #13943, #13942, #14386)

Performance

  • Code DB on LZ4: on a Glamsterdam devnet range of blocks that each read ~3.7 GB of 64 KiB code, mean block time fell from 2.58–2.63 s to 1.70–1.72 s and the slowest block from 7.8 s to 5.3 s (measured on LZ4-recompacted files); point reads of large values 88–93 µs → 47–49 µs; the code DB shrank 475 MB → 303 MB. New and compacted SST files use LZ4. (#13907)
  • Large-contract blocks: missed code is copied once (−31% block time, −50% allocations on a 58k × 64 KiB block); code reads no longer fill the RocksDB row cache, which is turned off for the code DB. (#14086)
  • Payload start-up: median first-payload latency 66.8 ms → 5.4 ms with the pipeline warm-up (process start to first VALID +0.8 s; disable with Init.PipelineWarmupEnabled=false). The ~2 s KZG trusted-setup load is no longer on the startup critical path. (#13931, #13998)
  • JSON-RPC: generated writers for blocks/transactions/logs (−13–27% time, up to −93% allocations), fewer passes over request and batch bodies, allocation-free filter binding, newHeads serialized once for all subscribers. (#14299, #14187, #14197, #14198, #14195, #13894)
  • RLP: built-in transaction types encode/decode without virtual dispatch (legacy encode −29%, EIP-1559 encode −11%). (#14455)
  • EVM: a long series of interpreter micro-optimisations (frameless MLOAD/MSTORE, padded code copy without end-of-code checks, cheaper DUP/EXP/SUB/SIGNEXTEND, per-depth call frame reuse, cached EIP-7702 delegation targets). (#14028, #13896, #13893, #13878, #13802, #14139, #13799 and others)
  • Flat backend reads: a bloom filter lets read-only execution (eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_createAccessList, eth_simulateV1, traces) skip in-memory layers for slots none of them wrote (FlatDb.InMemorySnapshotBloomBitsPerKey, default 14). The carry-forward slot cache becomes a fixed 64 MB set-associative table. (#14094, #14330, #14027)
  • Tracing: streamed struct logs flush every 1 MiB so a slow reader no longer holds hundreds of MB per request; trace_filter stops once count traces are collected. (#14461, #13890)
  • Networking: inbound transaction admission is budgeted before decoding (16 MiB per peer, 64 MiB total), oversized broadcast transactions are skipped before decoding, eth/snap response request IDs are checked before decoding, and discovery runs on a plain UDP socket instead of DotNetty. (#14434, #13506, #14184, #14346)
  • Transaction pool: an underpriced replacement of a set-code, blob or frame transaction is rejected before its authorization signatures are recovered or its blob proofs checked. (#14577)
  • zkVM guests: dozens of ZisK/SP1 guest optimisations (precompile-backed 256-bit arithmetic, Keccak and SHA-256, register-based dispatch, cheaper trie and witness handling) and tests-zkevm v21.0.1. (#14232, #14217, #13975, #14402, #14118 and others)

⚠️ Breaking changes

If you run a node (config and startup)

  • JsonRpc.Host, JsonRpc.EngineHost and AdditionalRpcUrls host names are resolved and bound to their addresses. Before, any host that was not an IP literal or localhost made Kestrel listen on all interfaces. Now the node listens only on the addresses the name resolves to; if it cannot resolve or resolves to a wildcard address, JSON-RPC does not start (the node keeps running and logs the host). Migration: behind NAT or with public DNS, configure a local interface IP; with Docker service names, point health checks at the bind address; to keep listening on every IPv4 interface, set the host to 0.0.0.0 explicitly. IP literals, localhost, * and + are unchanged. (#13746)
  • Init.DiagnosticMode=VerifyTrie and FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true now run only their step and exit, instead of doing the work mid-boot and continuing into a normal start. Equivalent commands: nethermind verify-trie and nethermind import-flat-db. verify-trie reports its verdict through the exit code (and fails on a DB with no head); the import fails if there is nothing to import. Migration: run the import/verification as a one-off, then remove the setting before starting the node normally. (#13715)
  • KeyStore.BlockAuthorAccount whose key cannot be loaded is now a configuration error on nodes with mining enabled (Clique, AuRa and XDC stop at startup). Before, the node fell back to sealing with the node key. Nodes that leave it unset are unaffected. (#14290)
  • The node refuses to start when JsonRpc.WebSocketsPort equals the engine port and Init.WebSocketsEnabled=true. Before, it started without an Engine API and only logged a warning. Use a different WebSocketsPort. (#14285)
  • WebSocket and IPC connections process up to 16 requests concurrently (JsonRpc.WebSocketsProcessingConcurrency and JsonRpc.IpcProcessingConcurrency 1 → 16), so pipelined requests on one public connection can be answered out of order — match responses by id. A batch is still processed and answered in order. Authenticated/Engine connections, and IPC when JsonRpc.EnabledModules includes Engine, still process one request at a time. Migration: set the option to 1 if a client relies on ordering (for example, pipelined dependent blob transactions with consecutive nonces). (#14345)
  • Buffered struct-log traces are capped at 256 MiB of opcode log per transaction (new JsonRpc.MaxBufferedTraceLogSize); larger non-streamed traces are truncated like a caller limit. Set 0 for the previous unlimited behaviour. (#14460)
  • eth_sendRawTransactionSync concurrency is capped by the new JsonRpc.RpcTxSyncMaxConcurrentRequests (default 128; 0 disables). Calls over the cap fail immediately with -32005 (HTTP 503) before the transaction is submitted. (#13735)
  • TraceStore serves only the trace types it recorded and falls back to live tracing otherwise; with TraceStore.TraceTypes=Trace alone, trace_block and trace_filter now need historical state (configure Trace and Rewards to serve them from the store). On pruned nodes these can return a missing-state error instead of incomplete output. (#14123)
  • Log and metric changes: snap sync logs Phase 1 of 2 / State Sync (Phase 2 of 2, healing) instead of the misleading healing percentage (#14308, #14344); flat DB metric nethermind_carry_forward_slot_wipes is replaced by nethermind_carry_forward_slot_evictions (one eviction = one entry, do not reuse wipe thresholds) (#14027). Update dashboards and log alerts that match the old strings.
  • FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexTraceParallelism is deprecated in favour of JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism; a non-zero value still overrides it. (#14363)
  • A block that takes longer than 3 minutes to process is abandoned without a verdict (new Blocks.BlockProcessingTimeoutMs, default 180000; 0 disables). It applies only to the main block-processing loop, not to tracing, simulation or block production. The block is not marked invalid, engine_newPayload does not answer INVALID for it, and it can be processed again; each consecutive retry of the same block gets twice the time, up to 16×. The node logs Processing block took longer than ms; abandoned without a verdict at Error. Migration: on slow hardware that legitimately needs longer (for example, a full sync through unusually heavy historical blocks), raise the value or set it to 0. (#14487)

If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API

Parity-style trace_* (most changes follow the draft trace spec in execution-apis#890):

  • trace_get returns a single trace object or null, not an array. Its argument is one traceAddress path: [] is the root, ["0x6","0x0"] is the first child of child 6. Migration: read an object/null; to address by flat position, index the result of trace_transaction. (#13858)
  • Reverted frames in Parity traces (trace_*) now include result: {gasUsed, output} next to error: "Reverted" (CREATE included, without address/code). In 2.1 only error was present; exceptional halts still have no result. Error labels are renamed: Stack overflow → Out of stack, Access violation → Out of bounds, Static call violation → Mutable Call In Static Context, the generic Error for an EIP-3541 0xEF code prefix → Invalid code, and TransactionCollision → Contract address collision. This aligns Nethermind with Geth, Erigon and reth. Traces already saved by TraceStore keep the old labels until traced again. Migration: consumers that read "no result" as "failed" must check error; update any matching on the old labels. (#13981)
  • A CALL that fails its balance or call-depth precheck now appears as a failed frame in both callTracer (error: "insufficient balance for transfer" / "max call depth exceeded") and Parity output (Insufficient balance for transfer / Max call depth exceeded, no result). A CREATE that fails its precheck is reported the same way, and a colliding CREATE2 gets a failed frame with Contract address collision (callTracer gasUsed equals its gas). The parent's subtraces and later siblings' traceAddress shift accordingly. In vmTrace, the cost of such a CREATE now includes the gas it forwarded, and the operation after a collision starts with the gas actually left. This matches Geth and Erigon. (#13957, #13958)
  • vmTrace ex.store.key / ex.store.val are minimal hex quantities (0x0, 0x1) instead of a padded word / byte string. (#13780) DUPn now reports n + 1 push values (#13781); buffered mem.off is a number (#13940).
  • trace_filter validation: unknown members, negative after/count, and an unknown mode return -32602 (#14050, #13857); mode: "union" is now honoured and an empty fromAddress/toAddress array behaves like an omitted one, so some requests that returned [] now return records (#13857). A block hash is no longer accepted as fromBlock/toBlock — use the new blockHash member (#14111). Bounds past the head or reversed return -32602 (#14040, #13935). Post-merge blocks no longer produce zero-value reward records, which shifts pagination over PoS ranges (#13938).
  • pending is rejected (-32602) by trace_call, trace_callMany, trace_block, trace_replayBlockTransactions and trace_filter, instead of silently tracing latest. eth_* and debug_* are unchanged. (#13936)
  • trace_rawTransaction rejects a signed gas limit above JsonRpc.GasCap (-38026) instead of lowering it; raise the cap to trace larger transactions (#14060). It also validates the transaction like block inclusion (nonce, sender code, chain ID, fee cap vs base fee) instead of tracing it with the sender's nonce (#14091, #14048).
  • trace_transaction, trace_get and trace_replayTransaction return null for an unknown transaction instead of -32000, including transactions outside the TxLookupLimit window. (#13937, #14037)
  • trace_call / trace_callMany errors use the eth_simulateV1 codes (e.g. -38014 insufficient funds, -38015 batch over block gas limit) instead of -32000; messages are unchanged. A mismatched chainId is -32602. (#14158, #13956)
  • trace_call / trace_callMany calls without a price run with BASEFEE 0, as eth_call, debug_traceCall and eth_simulateV1 already did. A call with no fee fields, gasPrice 0, or both fee caps 0 used to see the block's base fee; in trace_callMany each unpriced call now gets BASEFEE 0 and each priced call the block's. A call whose execution depends on BASEFEE can therefore return a different output, vmTrace and stateDiff. Migration: set gasPrice or maxFeePerGas to trace against the block's base fee. (#14045)

Other JSON-RPC:

  • Call objects with both data and input set to different values are rejected with -32602. Send calldata in input (or both, equal). An explicit null input no longer clears calldata given in data, and an explicit null for accessList, blobVersionedHashes or authorizationList no longer selects a transaction type. (#14089, #14049, #13897)
  • eth_sendTransaction (node wallet) on a post-London network with zero base fee rejects gasPrice: 0x0 / maxFeePerGas: 0x0. Send a non-zero fee or sign locally and use eth_sendRawTransaction. (#14375)
  • eth_sendRawTransactionSync timeouts return EIP-7966 error code 4 with the transaction hash in data, instead of -32016 without data, so a client can keep polling for the receipt. (#13820)
  • Blob calls without a positive maxFeePerBlobGas run at a blob base fee of 0 in eth_call, eth_estimateGas, trace_call and trace_callMany (Geth behaviour). (#14092)
  • eth_simulateV1 drops logs from reverted inner frames while keeping log indices aligned with Geth. (#13979, #14062)
  • eth_call / eth_estimateGas report precompile input failures with go-ethereum's error text; eth_estimateGas no longer reports them as gas required exceeds allowance. (#14281)
  • debug_setHead / debug_resetHead are now guarded rewinds: pause with admin_pauseBlockProcessing and let processing drain first, then resume with admin_resumeBlockProcessing. While paused, every engine_forkchoiceUpdated returns SYNCING (including with payload attributes), so the node builds no payloads until resumed. (#13558)
  • Engine API: engine_newPayloadV3+ rejects omitted or null payload fields; engine_newPayloadV3/V4 outside their fork window return Unsupported fork (incomplete payloads there get invalid params); a forkchoice to a processed block whose state was pruned no longer moves the head, and a resubmitted known block whose state was pruned is re-executed instead of answered VALID. (#14025, #14024, #14131, #14366, #13686)

If you build against Nethermind (plugin / library authors)

These are source-breaking changes: rebuild your plugins against 2.2.0.

  • IReadOnlyStateProvider.GetCode and IWorldStateScopeProvider.ICodeDb.GetCode return ReadOnlyMemory instead of byte[] (default = not served). (#14086)
  • BlockForRpc.Transactions is typed as BlockTransactions (hashes or full transactions). (#14299)
  • Built-in transaction decoders are no longer generic over the transaction type and drop their protected virtual hooks; BaseAccessListTxDecoder and OptimismLegacyTxDecoder are removed (LegacyTxDecoder takes allowEmptySignature). (#14455)
  • ICommitter / IBlockCommitter quota methods are replaced by TryEnableParallelCommit / SupportsParallelCommit; the quota constructor parameter is removed from FlatStorageTree and AbstractMinimalCommitter. (#13988)
  • WaitHandleExtensions (WaitOneAsync) is removed. (#13945)
  • TxPoolTxSource.GetOrderedTransactions (protected virtual) takes an additional IReleaseSpec spec parameter; overrides must add it. (#14304)
  • Custom ITxTracer implementations receive paired instruction callbacks (ReportOperationRemainingGas only after a reported StartOperation; resumes via ReportGasUpdateForVmTrace). (#13551)
  • Init steps can be declared as standalone commands with [StepCommand]; a step carrying it never runs during a normal start. (#13715)

Consensus / protocol (prototype forks only)

  • The EIP-8272 recent-root contract moves to 0x8272D9679689Ea2f307140CdF9002D27dC00Ffff and is deployed by an ordinary pre-signed transaction instead of being installed at activation; the EIP-8250 nonce manager and EIP-8141 expiry verifier follow the same model. (#14437, #14438, #14378)
  • EIP-7708 finalization logs are emitted in destroy order. Not observable on any shipped configuration (Amsterdam enables EIP-8246, which suppresses them). (#13568)

Default and configuration changes

Diffed I*Config.cs defaults and Nethermind.Runner/configs/*.json between 2.1.0 and 2.2.0.

Changed defaults

Key 2.1.0 2.2.0 PR
JsonRpc.WebSocketsProcessingConcurrency 1 16 #14345
JsonRpc.IpcProcessingConcurrency 1 16 #14345
Db.CodeDbRowCacheSize (hidden) 16 MiB unset (no row cache) #14086
Db.CodeDbRocksDbOptions (hidden) Snappy (inherited) compression=kLZ4Compression; prepended #13907

New settings

Key Default Purpose PR
Sync.ReconstructFinalizedStateFromBlockAccessLists true Rebuild finalized ancestors from verified BALs instead of executing them (EIP-7928 chains only) #14157
Init.PipelineWarmupEnabled true Warm the payload pipeline before RPC opens #13931
JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism 4 Node-wide parallel block-trace budget #13906, #14363
JsonRpc.MaxBufferedTraceLogSize 268435456 (256 MiB) Cap on non-streamed struct-log size per tx; 0 = unlimited #14460
JsonRpc.RpcTxSyncMaxConcurrentRequests 128 Cap on concurrent eth_sendRawTransactionSync; 0 disables #13735
FlatDb.DeferStorageTrieCommit true Write storage trie nodes after the block is reported valid #14058
FlatDb.ApplyStorageWritesOnIdleThread true Apply committed storage writes on an idle-priority thread #14059
FlatDb.MaxInMemorySnapshotBytes 0 (off) Byte budget for the in-memory snapshot window #13972
FlatDb.InMemorySnapshotBloomBitsPerKey 14.0 Negative filter for read-only slot reads; 0 disables #14094
SendPolicy.Enabled / RulesPath / JournalPath / WarnOnly false / null / null / false SendPolicy plugin #14396
TxPool.FrameTx* (9 keys) — EIP-8141 frame-transaction pool limits (prototype) #12526 and follow-ups
Blocks.PreWarmHandoff, Blocks.PrefetchBlockAccessListCode (hidden) true, false Prewarmer hand-off; BAL code prefetch #14312
Blocks.BlockProcessingTimeoutMs 180000 (3 min) Abandon a block that takes longer to process, without a verdict; each retry gets twice the time (up to 16×); 0 disables #14487

Deprecated: FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexTraceParallelism (hidden; use JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism). Removed keys: none.

Bundled configs: new mainnet_aztec.json; sync pivots refreshed for op-mainnet, op-sepolia, worldchain-mainnet, worldchain-sepolia; OP Superchain chainspecs refreshed (#13944, #14231). Chains/hoodi.json gains amsterdamTime and beaconChainGenesisTimestamp.

Sync, database & state

  • A block access list sync stops at the EIP-7928 activation block instead of scanning back to genesis. (#14368)
  • Snap sync warns when a restart discards existing flat state and reports how long the wipe took. (#14297)
  • Account wipes survive BAL healing; TreeSync node dependencies are resolved atomically. (#14156, #14051)
  • Unanchored forks stay out of bulk snapshot conversion; carry-forward generation is rechecked after a cache hit. (#13997, #14026)
  • A periodic log line reports how far the head is behind the chain tip and the estimated catch-up time. (#10892)
  • The flat import reports progress at Info every 60 s. (#13724)
  • During snap sync, a flat-DB node answers JSON-RPC reads of latest at once with a missing-state error, instead of retrying for 5 s and failing with -32603. (#14635)

JSON-RPC & tracing

  • eth_call, eth_estimateGas and eth_createAccessList treat a null or zero JsonRpc.GasCap as uncapped instead of failing every request. (#14001)
  • eth_createAccessList fills the missing half of a fee pair: the suggested priority fee next to a maxFeePerGas, or the priority fee plus twice the base fee next to a maxPriorityFeePerGas. (#14377)
  • Code written during a call replaces a stateOverride code override for the rest of the call in eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_simulateV1, trace_call and debug_traceCall. (#14114)
  • eth_simulateV1 on Amsterdam applies the blobBaseFee and movePrecompileToAddress overrides, and simulated blocks carry a slot number, so SLOTNUM works. (#14057, #13688)
  • eth_getLogs rejects a reversed range that ends at block zero (latest to earliest) with -32602, as it already did for other reversed ranges. (#13999)
  • trace_block and trace_replayBlockTransactions return [] for the genesis block instead of header not found. (#13783, #13801)
  • trace_filter address filters match rewards by their author, and match a failed CREATE only by its creator. (#13800, #14039)
  • trace_call / trace_callMany reject a priority fee above the fee cap with eth_call's reason; debug_traceCall rejects state and stateDiff overrides for the same account. (#14046, #14359)
  • Streamed traces that fail return a complete error instead of a truncated success. An unknown JavaScript tracer name is rejected before a JavaScript engine is created, and ctx.txIndex reports the transaction's position in its block. (#13666, #13529, #14249)
  • TraceStore reads stored vmTrace and stateDiff traces, selects them like live replay, and serves stored transaction traces only from canonical blocks. (#14093, #14115, #14122)
  • RPC metrics and stats use the dispatched method name, so whitespace variants no longer create separate labels. (#14194)

Engine API & block processing

  • engine_getPayloadV3 / V4 choose their fork window by whether execution requests are enabled, not by EIP-7623. (#13833)
  • A block engine_newPayload has already accepted stays queued for processing when the request's time budget runs out; the request still answers SYNCING. (#14337)
  • At startup, a side branch with no ancestor state is dropped instead of re-executing genesis on an empty state. (#14324)
  • The transaction pool re-adds the transactions of every block the head rewinds past. (#14492)
  • The pre-merge block producer is stopped on shutdown. (#14168)

Networking & protocol

  • discv4: Ping forward compatibility, verified ENRs retained for mismatched PING endpoints, EIP-1459 DNS tree-root signatures verified, second Hello disconnects the peer, a pong completes a ping only when it comes from the pinged endpoint. (#14151, #14277, #14183, #13832, #14576)
  • Concurrent node-filter acceptance is serialised; rejected peer candidates back off. (#14381, #14190)

Stability & hardening

  • .NET libraries updated to the October 2026 servicing release, which carries Microsoft's security fixes (.NET 10.0.13 CVE list) (#14628):
    • 10.0.12 → 10.0.13: Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection, Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.Extensions, Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Embedded, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console, Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool, System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager, System.IO.Hashing, System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData
    • 2.0.12 → 2.0.13: System.CommandLine
    • 10.0.401 → 10.0.402 (build-time only): Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git, Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub
  • Nethermind.RocksDbBindings updated to the stable 11.8.1.153. (#14617)
  • Docker images run on .NET 10.0.13: runtime base aspnet:10.0.13-resolute (and -resolute-chiseled), build SDK 10.0.402, so the runtime and ASP.NET Core fixes of the same servicing release ship in the images too. (#14632)

L2 & other chains

  • Optimism: Jovian operator fee and DA footprint reported in receipts (#13811); the sequencer's error is returned when forwarding eth_sendRawTransaction (#13815); EIP-1559 params with zero elasticity and a non-zero denominator are rejected (#13816).
  • Taiko: Shasta headers whose extraData is not exactly 7 bytes are rejected. (#13817)
  • XDC: XDPoS_getV2Block* header encoding and XDPoS_getMissedRoundsInEpochByBlockNum before the V2 switch fixed. (#14175, #14008)
  • Shutter: missed keys are counted atomically. (#14238)
