Important

Sepolia: Glamsterdam activated on Tue, 06 Oct 2026, 13:53:36 UTC. Sepolia nodes must run 2.1.0 or later.

Note

Upgrading from 1.39.x? The breaking changes below cover 2.0.0 → 2.1.0 only. Apply the 2.0.0 breaking changes and upgrade checklist first; they are the complete 1.39.x → 2.0 list.

For most nodes this is an in-place upgrade with no resync. Read Breaking changes first if you run on the flat backend with a custom sync config, run poacore, run a Flashbots relay, parse Parity-style traces, or build plugins against Nethermind.

Highlights

  • Glamsterdam on Sepolia. Final EIP-8037 state-gas rules, the TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT transaction cap, and Engine API alignment for Amsterdam. (#13140, #13484, #13627, #13554, #13583, #13586, #13755)
  • Faster EVM. The interpreter loop is replaced by tail-call chain dispatch, stack words stay in UInt256 limb layout, storage values stay as UInt256 until they are persisted, and JUMPDEST analysis is rewritten. (#13128, #13323, #13420, #13189, #13810)
  • Lower engine_newPayload latency. The response goes out as soon as the block has executed and its roots match, before the commit. engine_forkchoiceUpdated still waits for that head's commit. GC pauses no longer stall payloads the way they did. (#13647, #13711, #13476, #13334)
  • Per-transaction changeset index for flat archives (opt-in). A single-transaction trace starts at its target transaction instead of replaying the whole block before it: debug_traceTransaction went from ~7.1 s to ~28 ms in the PR's measurements. Whole-block traces run their transactions in parallel (6–10× faster). Enable with FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexEnabled=true. (#13454, #13426)
  • BAL healing after snap sync (flat backend). On the flat backend, the state left by snap sync is healed by replaying block access lists instead of downloading trie nodes. It is on by default (Sync.BalHealing=true); set it to false to go back to trie-node healing. snap/2 is advertised only when BAL healing can run. (#12945)
  • Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 networking. RLPx, discv4 and discv5 listen on both families, ENRs advertise both, and there is a new Network.ExternalIpV6 override. (#12679, #12982, #12983, #13731)
  • Flat backend safety rails. A flat DB that RocksDB had to auto-repair is now re-synced instead of trusted. Unsafe flat activations are refused at start instead of silently corrupting or discarding state. (#13645, #13644)
  • Reclaim the patricia trie after a trie→flat conversion. FlatDb.DropPruningTrieState=true deletes the old trie store on the next start once the flat DB owns the state (~227 GB on mainnet). Off by default. (#13572)
  • RocksDB 11 through Nethermind's own bindings. The RocksDB package is replaced with Nethermind.RocksDbBindings (RocksDB v10 → v11): source-generated P/Invoke with no marshalling stubs, and every native handle held in a SafeHandle. (#12853)
  • New EF bootnodes. The EF bootnode entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi are replaced with the new NodeOps fleet: five dual-stack nodes running both discv4 and discv5. (#13313)
  • More zkVM targets. Stateless guests for SP1 and OpenVM ship alongside ZisK, and the ZisK toolchain moves to 1.3.0-alpha. (#13435, #13769, #13743)

Performance

  • EVM dispatch and call frames: 3.8–4.5% faster block processing on the superblocks, realblocks and fusaka benchmark sets. (#13189)
  • Storage values held as UInt256: SLOAD 9–18%, SSTORE 42% and TSTORE ~50% faster, with no allocations on those paths. (#13420)
  • EVM stack in limb layout: 45–53% faster ADD, 16–36% faster SUB, and 9–18% faster shifts. (#13323)
  • JUMPDEST analysis: worst-case analysis of 64 KiB initcode (a 200 MGas block of PUSH1/JUMPDEST patterns) drops from 0.4–3.2 s to 22–153 ms, depending on the SIMD tier. Initcode is analysed on first use. (#13810)
  • Trie and storage-key hashing: 35–80% less time on transaction and receipt-root workloads. (#13552)
  • Prewarming: a single fan-out while senders arrive gives superblocks processing a median −4.4%, P99 −27.9%, and +7.6% MGas/s. Prewarming and trie concurrency caps are removed, and parallel work is budgeted across the state root, blooms, the receipts root and prewarming (2–4% faster processing). (#13640, #13388, #13770)
  • Carried caches: pre-block account and storage caches are carried across blocks. (#13100)
  • Discovery traffic: on a warm-started Hoodi node, discovery traffic fell by 90% (152 KiB/s → 15 KiB/s), and the standalone bootnode uses ~44% less working set. (#13122)
  • Snap sync: downloads are bounded and overlap with response processing. Whale-storage verification in FlatTrieVerifier is parallelised. (#12623, #12615)
  • RPC: eth_call, eth_estimateGas and eth_createAccessList no longer hash the transaction on every run (~0.2 ms on large calldata) (#13804). The stream interpreter is off by default because it lost on every measured eth_call shape. eth_getFilterChanges is served from shared block logs. (#12999, #13742)
  • Intel hybrid CPUs: block processing is pinned to the performance cores by default (Blocks.ProcessingCores). Nothing changes on other CPUs. (#13717)

⚠️ Breaking changes

If you run a node (config and startup)

  • poacore / poacore_validator now ship FlatDb.Enabled=false because they use FastSync without SnapSync (#13644). A node on those configs that synced on 2.0.0 is on the flat backend, since flat is 2.0.0's default. On 2.1.0 it refuses to start (Refusing --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat DB). Either pass --FlatDb.Enabled=true, or delete the flat, flatHistory and persistedSnapshot directories and resync the state.
  • --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat DB is refused. In 2.0.0 the node silently discarded the state and resynced (#13428). It now stops with an error. (#13644)
  • Flat + Sync.FastSync=true + Sync.SnapSync=false is refused on a fresh node. Legacy tree sync on the flat backend can leave holes in the state. An already-synced node keeps running and logs a warning. The exception is importing from patricia (FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true on a datadir that holds patricia state). (#13644)
  • New FlatDb.OnRepair setting, default Resync. If RocksDB auto-repairs the flat DB, the node now wipes the flat state and runs state sync again. Headers, bodies and receipts are kept. Archive nodes synced from genesis cannot snap-resync. Set FlatDb.OnRepair=Ignore and plan a resync yourself if a repair is ever reported. (#13645)
  • Receipt.MaxBlockDepth default raised back from 1,000 to 10,000, and the limit is now also enforced on eth_getFilterLogs. On nodes with the log index, only blocks the index cannot serve count towards the limit. A filter created by eth_newFilter over a wider range is still accepted, but eth_getFilterLogs on it fails with -32602. (#13131)
  • Removed config keys: FlatDb.EnablePreimageRecording, Db.PreimageDbRocksDbOptions, Db.PreimageDbAdditionalRocksDbOptions (#13690), LogIndex.VerifyRpcResponse (#13131), and Grpc.Enabled, Grpc.Host, Grpc.Port along with the gRPC endpoint (#13330). A JSON config that still sets them logs Invalid configuration settings at startup. Remove them from configs, environment variables and command-line flags.
  • Merge.CompactMemory default changed from Yes to No. This removes GC compaction stalls from engine_newPayload. Steady-state RSS may be somewhat higher. (#13476)
  • Init.LogRules no longer routes to Seq, and Seq.MinLevel is now the floor for the Seq target. To send a namespace's Trace output to Seq, add an explicit writeTo="seq" rule in NLog.config. (#13419)
  • Dual-stack by default. With Network.LocalIp unset, the P2P TCP and discovery UDP listeners now try to bind [::] on Linux and Windows, so the P2P port may now be reachable over IPv6. Check your firewall. macOS stays IPv4-only. Set Network.LocalIp=0.0.0.0 to keep IPv4-only. (#12982)
  • Pruning.FullPruningTrigger=VolumeFreeSpace with a threshold too low to ever trigger now logs a startup warning. Automatic pruning was already not running in that case, so nothing new is broken. (#13485)

If you run a Flashbots relay

  • Flashbots.EnableValidation now defaults to true. flashbots_validateBuilderSubmissionV3 checks the submitted block's state root, receipts root, gas used and logs bloom against its execution. Set it to false explicitly to get the old behaviour. (#13452)

If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API

  • eth_getHeaderByNumber("pending") returns null, matching go-ethereum and execution-apis#877. (#13082)
  • proof_getTransactionByHash / proof_getTransactionReceipt return result: null for a transaction they cannot serve, instead of a -32000 error. proof_getTransactionReceipt returns -32002 when the block can no longer be retraced. (#13366)
  • Parity vmTrace stack pushes are hex quantities (0x0, 0x1), not byte strings. Word operations now report their pushes. (#13750, #13487)
  • Other trace output changes. Empty trace selections are accepted. trace_get keeps lookup errors instead of replacing them. trace_filter returns an error when the requested history is unavailable, and buffered trace_filter now applies a single JsonRpc.Timeout to the whole request. Deleted-account fields carry deletion markers. callTracer omits to on a failed top-level CREATE. (#13667, #13676, #13677, #13668, #13078)
  • EIP-3155 / structLogs traces are corrected: gasUsed is the top-level execution-gas delta, refunds are cumulative, and opcode names follow Geth (0x44 is reported as DIFFICULTY). (#12981)
  • eth_estimateGas runs entirely against the requested block, the way eth_call does, with a single deterministic search. Before, the first run used a synthetic next-block header. Estimates can differ from 2.0.0 within the error margin. Invalid-opcode and stack failures now return the standard error texts (for example invalid opcode: INVALID, stack underflow (0 <=> 2)), and eth_call uses the same texts. (#13899)
  • eth_call with maxPriorityFeePerGas above maxFeePerGas (after London) fails before any gas is bought, with the same max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas error execution returns. eth_createAccessList fills the fee cap as the priority fee plus twice the base fee when only a priority fee is given. (#13904)
  • Call requests with gasPrice and a type-specific field (accessList, blobVersionedHashes, authorizationList) but no explicit type are no longer decoded as legacy transactions. eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_createAccessList and eth_simulateV1 results change for those requests. (#13450)
  • eth_subscribe("logs") delivers logs for every block that becomes canonical, and removed: true logs for every block that leaves the canonical chain. A subscriber that falls more than 1,000 blocks behind (or 10,000 events for pending-transaction and peer subscriptions) is disconnected. (#13451)
  • No state for a block now returns -32002 from every method, and guard-rail rejections (-32002, -32005, 4444) are no longer logged at WARN. (#13643)
  • The SSZ-REST Engine API moves from /engine/v2/... to /engine/v1/..., per execution-apis#793. The JSON-RPC engine_* surface is unchanged. (#13023)
  • engine_newPayload rejects a post-Shanghai payload with a null withdrawals list (MissingWithdrawals). (#13501)
  • /data/events accepts ?events=. A client that only needs processing statistics should pass ?events=processed. (#13334)

If you build against Nethermind (plugin / library authors)

These are source-breaking changes: rebuild your plugins against 2.1.0.

  • IBackgroundTaskScheduler.TryScheduleTask now takes a request type that implements IBackgroundTaskRequest, and the source string is gone. (#9956)
  • ISyncPeerPool.Free is removed. SyncPeerAllocation is now IDisposable, so dispose it with using. (#13094)
  • World-state scopes are opened with TryBeginScope / TryBeginScopeAtTarget, which return false for an unavailable base instead of throwing. (#13522)
  • Storage APIs take UInt256 values instead of byte arrays. SlotValue is removed. (#13420)
  • EVM extension API: the gas-policy methods are TryConsume*, the OutOfGas flag is removed, and the EvmStack constructors require a CodeInfo. (#13189)
  • ProcessingOptions.Trace is removed. Use TraceProcessingOptions.ReadOnlyReplay. (#13443)
  • Value-hash and protocol API changes in the txpool and networking code. (#13592)
  • Nullable reference types are enabled in EVM, Trie, State and 7 foundation projects. (#13099, #12155)

Consensus / protocol

  • Glamsterdam (Amsterdam-gated, Sepolia from 10-06): the EIP-8037 spill is repaid after a child frame merges, and a restored spill is burnt on a top-level halt (#13140, #13484). TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT (2³² − 1) is enforced in the pool, in block validation and in eth_estimateGas (#13627). The unknown-original storage flag is kept across repeated writes (#13554). The EL no longer enforces slot ordering on engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4 (#13583). Orphaned headers are checked for a slot number (#13586). engine_getPayloadV5 is rejected from Amsterdam on (#13755). EIP-7928 receipt event metadata is corrected (#13509), and AuRa keeps existing accounts in BAL preprocessing (#13047).
  • XDC: randomize-contract transactions now pay and burn gas (#13359), and sign-transaction receipts are encoded as legacy in the receipts trie. The receipts change fixes a consensus divergence on typed transactions (#13375).

Sync, database & state

  • Recovery of missing contract code. (#9417)
  • A fast-sync body could be dropped by the block cache, which left the receipts stage stuck. Fixed. Nodes already stuck on this need a bodies resync. (#13474)
  • Flat persistence keeps going when the committed state is off the canonical chain. MinReorgDepth stays reachable after folding to the finalized boundary. Flat state is retained across Engine-X reorgs. (#13591, #13550, #13402)
  • A gather whose state was just persisted is retried instead of refused (fixes an occasional -32002 No state available at the block being folded). (#13763)
  • VerifyWithTrie no longer reports a false positive when an account is deleted that the trie still holds. (#13521)
  • debug_resetHead prunes flat snapshots that are unreachable from the new head. (#13524)
  • New FlatDb.EnableCarryForwardCache (default true) to turn off the cross-head read cache. (#13752)
  • The history-walk ETA overflow no longer kills progress or discards a finished archive-proof walk (this bug is present in 2.0.0). The walk also reports the replay block of a storage range. (#13761, #13791, #13604, #13754, #13620)
  • SyncServer range broadcasts are serialised. Pooled lists from trie path recovery are disposed. (#12728, #13266)
  • ElapsedMicroseconds overflow on long-running stopwatches fixed. (#13416)
  • The history pruner is created before the block processor starts. (#13285)
  • When a block wipes a contract's storage, the pre-block storage cache now invalidates only that contract. Before, it dropped the whole cache and logged an Info line each time, which on pre-Cancun history meant tens of thousands of lines an hour during a full sync from genesis. (#13850)
  • The disk-space probe is skipped when the availability check is disabled. (#13456)
  • Code from a reverted CREATE no longer reaches the code DB, and code-write counters roll back with it. (#13074, #13432, #13433)

JSON-RPC & tracing

  • Malformed JSON-RPC batch items no longer abort the rest of the batch. (#12537)
  • eth_syncing reports the beacon tip as the highest block. (#12739)
  • debug_traceTransactionByBlockAndIndex resolves block tags and hashes. (#13138)
  • eth_feeHistory reward percentiles use post-refund receipt gas. (#13563)
  • eth_sendRawTransactionSync no longer misses a receipt included in the next block. (#13736)
  • Simulation cache is reset when the real chain advances. (#13444)
  • Single-transaction traces no longer replay the transactions after the target. (#13426)
  • Discarded block traces in debug_traceTransactionInBlockByIndex are disposed. (#13324)
  • EIP-7708 finalization logs are reported to tracers, and the previous transient value shows up in TSTORE traces. (#13567, #13504)
  • Account-creation results are preserved in traced and BAL-backed execution. (#13574)
  • eth_simulateV1 child headers and payload attributes inherit the parent slot number (for Amsterdam SLOTNUM). (#13584, #13585)

Engine API & block processing

  • engine_forkchoiceUpdated waits for the head's own commit, including when blocks are queued behind it, a second copy of the head is queued, or the commit is slow. (#13711)
  • Fixed a missed drain of the block processing queue. (#13749)
  • Null required Cancun payload fields are rejected. (#13747)
  • Custody columns are applied on forkchoiceUpdatedV5. (#13109)
  • FOCIL: engine_getInclusionListV1 accepts the parent block hash. (#13097)
  • The block processor is split into a main-only BlockchainProcessor and a separate OneTimeChainProcessor, with a follow-up fix for transaction-index replay. (#13449, #13629)
  • Blocks are processed while sender recovery finishes. (#13597)

Networking & protocol

  • A Hello whose node ID differs from the authenticated peer is rejected. (#13348)
  • Outgoing receipts are capped under the devp2p message size limit. Trie-node and receipts requests have bounded lookups. The receipt log limit is derived from the block gas ceiling. (#13595, #13596, #13288)
  • Connect workers no longer dial past MaxActivePeers. (#13302)
  • Discovery event loop shutdown is bounded. (#13617)
  • Startup external-IP resolution retries before it gives up. Persisted peers keep the endpoint that was actually dialled. (#13731)

Stability & hardening

  • A malformed EthStats ping no longer terminates the node. (#13353)
  • BN254 Add/Mul input length is checked in release builds. (#13208)
  • Keccak output sizes the sponge cannot serve are rejected. (#13187)
  • A stateless rejection no longer terminates DEBUG-enabled hosts. Execution requests are recovered correctly in stateless RPC inputs. (#13535, #13346)
  • The Docker images carry Nethermind's OCI labels (source, revision, version) instead of Ubuntu's. (#13694)

L2 & other chains

  • XDC: nine XDC-specific eth_* methods are added (block signers and finality, candidates, staking ROI, token stats) (#12950). XDPoS header fields are returned over JSON-RPC and newHeads, and AuRa's step and signature are restored on newHeads (#13055). eth_getAccountInfo returns the XDC shape (#13228). Transactions under the minimum gas price are rejected at pool admission (#13222). eth_gasPrice is floored at the pool minimum (#13633). SyncInfo QC and TC are verified independently (#13296). Unsupported eth versions are no longer advertised (#13018). State sync starts without waiting for headers back to genesis (#13609).
  • Optimism: after Jovian, payload attributes from op-node (8-byte eip1559Params plus a separate minBaseFee) are accepted. Before, every engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3 with attributes failed with -38003, which broke block building behind op-node (#13813). Blocks Nethermind builds after Isthmus now keep the L2ToL1MessagePasser storage root as withdrawalsRoot instead of the empty-list root, which op-geth and Nethermind itself reject (#13814). OP Superchain chain registry refreshed (#13043, #13179, #13430, #13606).
  • Taiko: Taiko mainnet (Alethia) uses the 0.01 gwei Shasta base-fee floor that taiko-geth and alethia-reth enforce. Before, Nethermind rejected current Alethia blocks with Invalid baseFee (#13812). Unzen zk-gas metering for failed steps matches REVM, so canonical blocks that end a step out of gas are no longer rejected (#13824).
  • Plataberget: new archive config, --config plataberget_archive. (#13073)

Full Changelog: 2.0.0...2.1.0

Release notes

669 merged pull requests since 1.39.3, from 39 contributors.

Nethermind 2.0.0 is a hardened, faster, archive-capable execution client, built for Ethereum, its L2s, and beyond. It consolidates everything shipped in 2.0.0-rc and 2.0.0-rc2.

Most nodes upgrade in place with no resync. There are breaking changes — read Breaking changes before upgrading, especially if you run an archive node, set custom config keys, or build against Nethermind as a library or plugin.

Important

Upgrading from 1.39.x? This page is the complete list of breaking changes from 1.39.x to 2.0. It replaces the 2.0.0-rc and 2.0.0-rc2 notes; the 2.0.0-rc release page has been removed. Go through Breaking changes and the Upgrade checklist below.

Going straight to 2.1.0 or later? Apply this list first, then the 2.1.0 breaking changes.

⚠️ Breaking changes

If you run a node (config)

  • Db.FlushOnExit is now an enum, not a boolean. Values: None, WalOnly, Full. The default changes from full-flush to WalOnly. If your config, env var, or CLI still sets true/false, the node fails to start — change true → Full, false → None.
  • Blocks.PreWarmStateOnBlockProcessing was replaced by Blocks.PreWarming. New enum values: None, Block, BlockAndMempool (default BlockAndMempool). The old key is now silently ignored (you'll get a warning, not a crash) — rename it or you lose your setting.
  • Numeric config keys are now unsigned. Negative values are rejected and the node fails to start. The one common case: Receipt.TxLookupLimit: -1 (the old "never index" sentinel) must become 18446744073709551615.
  • Receipt.MaxBlockDepth default lowered from 10000 → 1000. A single eth_getLogs spanning more than 1000 blocks is now rejected unless the log index is enabled. If you rely on wide ranges: raise Receipt.MaxBlockDepth, split the query, or enable the log index. 2.1.0 restores the 10,000 default (#13131).
  • FlatDb.HistoryRetention is required whenever you set a window size or a since-block. FlatDb.HistoryRetentionBlocks on its own fails to start. A window size without a mode, Rolling without a size, SinceBlock without a block, or both numbers at once, are all refused.
  • A configured FinalTotalDifficulty is no longer treated as "TTD reached" (#12555). Custom-FTD configs that relied on that inference will wait for the real TTD.
  • sepolia and hoodi default configs are now discv5-only (hoodi's static bootnode list was removed). Stock-config nodes on those networks discover peers via discv5 + DNS. Custom DiscoveryConfig is unaffected.
  • Mainnet ancient-history barrier raised (block 15537394 → 24600000). Existing nodes keep all their data. Only new or resyncing nodes retain less pre-24.6M history by default.

If you run an archive node

  • Archive configs now enable the flat-database backend with history (see New archive layout below). Your existing patricia archive DB keeps working (the new flag is ignored on an existing DB — nothing corrupts). To actually run the new flat archive you must resync, or set FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true for an in-place trie→flat import. Enabling flat history is forward-only — there is no backfill below the point you enable it.

If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API

  • engine_newPayloadV5: a malformed block-access-list envelope now returns {"status":"INVALID", ...} (HTTP 200) instead of JSON-RPC error -32602. (#13012)
  • trace_simulateV1: the response field stateChanges was renamed to stateDiff. (#12892)
  • Receipt JSON on the t8n / direct-serialization path now emits root or status (mutually exclusive), not both. The standard eth_getTransactionReceipt path is unchanged. (#12867)
  • debug_traceCall now uses a base fee of 0 for unpriced calls, matching go-ethereum. Reported gas figures change accordingly. (#12804)
  • eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas returned a gas price; it now returns a priority fee. (#13129)
  • eth_getStorageAt position parsing is stricter — spec-compliant hex-quantity clients are fine, but a client sending a bare number or un-prefixed string may now get a parse error. (Verify against your integrations.)
  • Amsterdam-gated (not active on mainnet yet, relevant if you test against devnets): eth_call now returns errors (out-of-gas, address collision, EF-prefix) where it previously returned 0x; eth_estimateGas and eth_createAccessList return updated values. (#12806, #12971, #12970)

If you build against Nethermind (plugin / library authors)

  • Many IConfig numeric properties changed from long/int to ulong. This is source-breaking — recompile your plugins against 2.0.0.

Consensus / protocol

  • EIP-7610 support removed. (#12935) No change on any live network — the storage-collision check is superseded by EIP-684 and was never activated as a fork. Only affects state-test / collision fixtures.
  • Stricter RLPx/Snappy frame validation. (#12896) Malformed frames are now rejected/disconnected. Conformant peers (Geth, Besu, older Nethermind, CL relays) are unaffected — this is DoS hardening.
  • Optimism engine_signalSuperchainV1 V0 byte layout corrected (7→8 bytes) to match op-geth/op-node. (#12805) OP-Stack operators only.

Dropped

  • ethernity-sepolia network removed (ethernity-mainnet is retained).

Upgrade checklist

From 1.39.x

  1. Stop the node. No resync is needed for a normal full node, and your existing patricia database stays patricia — it is detected at start.
  2. Audit your config for the breaking keys above. The ones that crash on start are Db.FlushOnExit (bool→enum), any negative numeric value, Receipt.TxLookupLimit: -1, and FlatDb.HistoryRetentionBlocks without FlatDb.HistoryRetention.
  3. Rename Blocks.PreWarmStateOnBlockProcessing → Blocks.PreWarming (otherwise it is silently ignored).
  4. eth_getLogs users: check whether Receipt.MaxBlockDepth (now 1000) affects your queries.
  5. Archive operators: decide between keeping your existing patricia archive (works as-is) or resyncing/importing to the new flat archive with history.
  6. Plugin/library authors: recompile against 2.0.0 (IConfig numeric types changed).
  7. Fresh nodes will serve snap. Turn it off with Sync.SnapServingEnabled=false if that is not what you want.
  8. Start the node and confirm 2.0.0 in the startup logs.

From 2.0.0-rc / 2.0.0-rc2

No database-format change and no resync. Do step 2 above (the FlatDb.HistoryRetention requirement arrived in rc2), then start.

Do not set --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat datadir — see Known issues.

Known issues

These were open at release against the flat backend, which is the default for a new database. A node that upgraded in place from 1.39.x keeps its patricia backend and is not exposed to any of them. Where a later release addresses an item, it is noted.

  • A snap sync on the flat backend cannot resume across a restart. Every run clears the flat columns, so restarting mid-sync discards the state downloaded so far and starts again from zero. Plan an uninterrupted initial sync, or sync on --FlatDb.Enabled=false (patricia/half-path), which does resume. A node that has reached the tip never re-enters snap, so this affects bring-up only. (#13601)
  • Copy-style full pruning is not available on the flat backend. A flat node accepts Pruning.Mode=Hybrid, Pruning.FullPruningTrigger, and Pruning.FullPruningThresholdMb without warning but never prunes, and admin_prune reports disabled. If you depend on periodic full pruning, stay on the patricia backend for now. In-place upgrades from 1.39.x keep patricia and are unaffected. (#13600) From 2.1.0 the node logs a warning when an automatic full-pruning trigger is set on flat (#13644); pruning itself is still patricia-only.
  • Legacy (non-snap) state sync on the flat backend can produce a bad state. With Sync.SnapSync=false, a restart during state sync can leave permanent account/storage holes (the trie is complete, the flat leaf is missing), and pivot changes can leave stale storage subtrees. Both surface later as a deterministic HeaderGasUsedMismatch. Use snap sync (the default), or resync on the patricia backend. (#13575, #13576) From 2.1.0 a fresh node refuses flat + Sync.FastSync=true + Sync.SnapSync=false (#13644).
  • A RocksDB auto-repair of a corrupted flat DB can silently drop leaves. The node then resumes as "already have state" and diverges from consensus. If RocksDB reports that it repaired your database, resync rather than continue. (#13577) Fixed in 2.1.0: a repaired flat DB is re-synced by default (FlatDb.OnRepair=Resync, #13645).
  • --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat datadir silently discards the state and full-resyncs. The node does not refuse. The inverse (a patricia DB with the new flat default) is detected and protected. Do not pass that flag to an existing flat node. (#13428) Fixed in 2.1.0: the node refuses to start instead (#13644).

Two smaller JSON-RPC rough edges were also open at release: guard-rail rejections (-32002, -32005, 4444) still log one WARN per request (#13602), and "no state for that block" is answered with different error codes depending on the method (#13603). Both fixed in 2.1.0 (#13643).

Highlights

  • Flat DB is the default state backend (#11931). FlatDb.Enabled defaults to true. A new node, or a resync, gets the flat backend. An existing patricia database is detected at start and stays patricia — upgrading does not migrate or resync you. To sync a fresh node on patricia: --FlatDb.Enabled=false.
  • Flat-history archive (#12943). Archive-grade, header-verifiable history in four shapes (full, rolling window, since-block, per-address), all built from ordinary syncing — no separate archive database, no new P2P protocol. Below the retained floor, reads fail closed rather than silently answering from live state.
  • Historical eth_getProof on a flat archive (#13098). Off by default.
  • Streaming snapshot download (#12862). Import an archive snapshot without first storing the full archive locally, lowering peak disk during bring-up. Provision free disk equal to at least 1.5× the snapshot size; the import fails if less space is available.
  • Standalone bootnode tool (#12601). A dedicated discv4/discv5 bootnode with REST APIs, Prometheus metrics, and Docker/Grafana assets.
  • In-house discv5 (#11728), replacing the external implementation.
  • EIP-7805 (FOCIL) inclusion lists (#8003) and a sparse blob pool with eth/72 cell-level exchange + engine_getBlobsV4 (#11094). Both are implemented and fork-gated (they activate with their respective forks).

Fresh nodes on the default config also serve snap (Sync.SnapServingEnabled defaults on for the flat path). Set Sync.SnapServingEnabled=false if you do not want the extra outbound bandwidth. Existing patricia nodes are unaffected.

A patricia node upgraded to 2.0.0 will still create empty flat column families on disk (the probe opens them before it notices the patricia state). This is harmless extra disk and file descriptors; they are not used.

New archive layout

Running an archive node used to mean a heavyweight, separate database and a lot of disk. Nethermind 2.0.0 puts archive-grade history on the flat state database (#12943), and that changes the trade-offs:

  • No separate archive database, no new protocol. History is built up by ordinary syncing — the same node, the same peers. You don't run a different node type or transfer data between nodes.
  • Header-verifiable. The state root at any retained height can be reconstructed from the flat rows and checked against that block's header. Historical answers are provable, not best-effort.
  • You choose how much history you pay for. Four shapes, one feature:
    • Full archive — retain every historical state.
    • Rolling window (FlatDb.HistoryRetention=Rolling + FlatDb.HistoryRetentionBlocks) — answer historical queries for the last N blocks and reclaim older state.
    • Since a fixed height (FlatDb.HistoryRetention=SinceBlock + FlatDb.HistoryRetentionSinceBlock) — keep everything from a chosen block onward and never prune it.
    • Per-address (FlatDb.HistorySliceAddresses=…) — retain deep history only for the contracts you query while keeping the general window small.
  • Correct by design at the edges. Below the retained floor, reads fail closed with an explicit "not retained" response instead of silently answering from live state.
  • A competitive footprint. A full Ethereum mainnet archive is approximately 2.1 TB today, substantially smaller than legacy trie/hash-based archives.
  • Historical eth_getProof (#13098). An unwindowed flat archive can serve eth_getProof and proof_* at covered historical heights. Off by default.

The upshot: teams that previously ran a full archive "just in case" can instead use a bounded window — or retain deep history only for selected contracts — to reduce disk and operational overhead without giving up the historical answers they need.

How much disk to expect now

Measured on live nodes, mainnet at ~block 25.88M (2026-09-01). Numbers grow slowly as the chain grows — treat them as "today's floor," not a fixed ceiling.

Windowed mainnet archive ~2 months of state and ~1 year of blocks; block pruning measurement pending ~0.9 TB (926 GB; provisional) ~1.0 TB (provisional) 1.5 TB

Current measured saving: retaining ~2 months of state while keeping ~1 year of blocks takes the execution DB from ~2.1 TB → ~0.9 TB — roughly 60% less disk. The figure for a fully pruned ~2-month block window is still being measured.

Per-address disk scales with how active your chosen contracts are — pick lower-traffic contracts and it drops sharply. It's a "keep deep history cheaply" tool.

Rule of thumb for planning:

  • Need full mainnet history → provision 3 TB (~2.1 TB DB + CL + room to grow).
  • Only need recent history → the current measurement is ~0.9 TB for ~2 months of state with ~1 year of blocks retained. The fully pruned ~2-month figure is pending; size your window with FlatDb.HistoryRetention=Rolling + FlatDb.HistoryRetentionBlocks.
  • Need forever-history for a few specific contracts → budget by those contracts' activity, plus a small base window.

Performance

Flat state at chain tip

A 12-hour Ethereum mainnet measurement across six fully synced, warm nodes found the flat state layout to be the fastest configuration at chain tip on both hardware tiers. Against the same-tier 1.39.2 half-path baseline, flat processed blocks at 1.80× the throughput on 8 vCPU standard machines and 2.55× on 16 vCPU premium machines.

The comparison used three configurations — 2.0.0 flat, 2.0.0 half-path, and 1.39.2 half-path — on each hardware tier, all over the same 12-hour window. Each node contributed 2,880 samples and processed 3,587–3,588 blocks, with zero bad blocks, zero sample gaps, and zero restarts. RAM, storage, region, and OS image were identical; core count was the only hardware difference between tiers.

Mean block processing time at chain tip

The largest improvement is in tail latency, not the typical block. Flat's p99 was 351 ms on standard and 208 ms on premium — only 4.3× and 4.2× its own median. The 1.39.2 baseline reached 1,849 ms and 1,646 ms at p99, or 21× and 24× its median. 2.0.0 half-path also substantially reduced the tail, showing that part of the gain comes from 2.0.0 generally and part from the flat layout.

Median, p90, and p99 block processing time

Flat also benefited most from additional cores: mean processing time improved from 96.5 ms on 8 vCPU to 57.6 ms on 16 vCPU, a 1.67× improvement. The equivalent gain was 1.13× for 2.0.0 half-path and 1.18× for 1.39.2 half-path.

The trade-off is initial sync time. Flat took 192.0 minutes on standard and 128.6 minutes on premium — about 75% longer than the same-tier 1.39.2 half-path baseline. Once synced, it delivered the best and most consistent chain-tip performance measured here; 2.0.0 half-path was the fastest configuration to reach tip.

Time to sync to chain tip

Faster eth_call under load

Across the completed benchmark cells, 2.0.0 answers the internal 497-record eth_call corpus 15–27% faster than 1.39.3, with byte-identical responses on all 497 records in every layout and architecture measured. It also sustains 22–25% more heavy high-gas multicalls per second.

Both versions ran against the same mainnet snapshot at block 25,490,000, using the same seeded request sequences and runner, interleaved over overlay mounts on pristine snapshots. Figures come from the run-rpc-benchmarks workflow, measured on the 2.0.0-rc build; nothing on the eth_call path changed between that build and 2.0.0.

Latency on the 497-record corpus

The corpus represents heavy simulation traffic: every record carries state overrides, and the median request is about 331 KiB. Each arm replayed 20,000 seeded requests at 100 requests per second after a discarded 60-second warm-up.

eth_call latency percentiles, 1.39.3 vs 2.0.0

The gain widens into the tail on the flat layout: amd64 p99 drops 29.5%, from 104.79 ms to 73.92 ms. This reflects real work saved rather than scheduling luck — CPU time per request falls 25.5% on amd64 flat and 17.7% on arm64 flat. Paired per-record medians agree with the aggregate: −20.1% on amd64 (95% CI −20.6% to −19.6%; 451 of 497 records faster) and −25.2% on arm64 (95% CI −25.7% to −24.3%; 476 faster).

Throughput

Closed-loop throughput was measured over 40 passes across all 497 records at concurrency 16. Compared with 1.39.3, 2.0.0 delivered 29.6% more throughput on amd64 flat, 36.4% more on arm64 flat, and 20.6% more on amd64 halfpath.

Closed-loop eth_call throughput, 1.39.3 vs 2.0.0

Heavy high-gas multicalls

Three EthCallChaos high-gas Multicall3 aggregate3 scenarios — roughly 34 KB payloads carrying about 500 ms of EVM work each — ran in isolation at 100 and 300 requests-per-second targets, in ABBA order, with 512 virtual users. Both versions saturated at both target rates, so achieved throughput is the relevant measure; p99 values in the 19–37 second range represent queue depth, not call latency.

Heavy high-gas Multicall3 capacity, 1.39.3 vs 2.0.0

Repeats within a version varied by about 1 request per second, against a between-version gap of about 5 requests per second on flat and 3.5 on halfpath. Every multicall cell completed with zero failed requests, while the accompanying light eth_call contract mix remained sub-millisecond on both versions.

Other optimizations

  • Keccak-256 ~30% faster via AVX-512VL and batched hashing. (#12844)
  • Single-call RocksDB point reads remove a value-sized native allocation and copy on every read. (#12986)
  • EVM stops redundantly zeroing memory on overwrites and fresh allocations — large wins on memory-heavy execution. (#12953)
  • eth_call state overrides applied without merkleization. (#12904)
  • Precompile result cache is partitioned per precompile and bounded — a cheap precompile can no longer evict an expensive one, and the cache no longer grows without limit. (#12966)
  • JavaScript tracers are bounded per transaction. Each transaction gets its own V8 engine, released as soon as its result is rendered, so only one engine is alive at a time during a block trace. A native noopTracer is available. (#13464)
  • ARM64-specific: EVM byte-swap fast path (eth_call latency and block-processing improvements) and a per-thread EVM call-pool free list. (#12798, #12905)
  • Plus hot-path loop/atomics cleanups. (#13000, #12998, #12870, #12905)

Sync, database & state

  • Mainnet snap no longer livelocks on the last large-storage account; forced pivot updates are distance-guarded. (#13155, #13200 / #13310)
  • A stalled snap sync is now visible at the default log level. (#13248 / #13257)
  • In-flight sync dispatch is drained before the database is torn down, so a graceful restart of a syncing node no longer SIGSEGVs. (#13154 / #13309)
  • Shutdown no longer flushes the unfinalized tail to RocksDB. A clean restart used to leave the persisted state at an unfinalized block, making any reorg below the pre-shutdown head unservable. (#13523)
  • Fixed false header < body block-tree corruption after an ungraceful restart during beacon sync. (#12876)
  • Flat warmer correctness: isolate warmer misses and safely publish verified reads (resolves InvalidStateRoot waves); restore the trie-warmer negative cache without poisoning live reads; warmer misses no longer escape through shared trie children. (#12951, #12877, #13272)
  • A malformed snap AccountRange no longer strands a sync partition; a malformed header response no longer stalls fast-headers. (#12979, #13019)
  • Receipt bodies are looked up by number and hash. (#13139)
  • Compacted snapshots are released after base conversion; finalized forks are pruned from persisted snapshots. (#13223, #13230)
  • Full-pruning snapshot trigger is measured from the pruning boundary. (#13199 / #13308)
  • Fast-sync settings (pivot block, hash, and total difficulty) are refreshed for every supported network at release, so a fresh node starts from a pivot its peers still retain. (#12962)

JSON-RPC & Engine API

  • Streamed trace_* keeps the module rented until the result is written. Concurrent traces no longer collide on the overridable world scope. (#13095)
  • Unauthenticated input no longer produces empty HTTP 500s, leaked stack traces in error.data, or a WARN flood of -32602s. A chunk-size ≥ 0x80000000 is HTTP 400. Deep recursive eth_estimateGas no longer answers -32603 "Stack empty." (#13194, #13195, #13197, #13198, #13156 / #13251)
  • A missing-argument marker on a required parameter is rejected as -32602, not an NRE. (#13235)
  • Out-of-memory on the RPC path is logged without formatting the request. (#13225)

  • Each engine_getPayload response is built from a single block candidate; the improvement context of a replaced payload is disposed. (#13093, #13206)
  • Browser POSTs are routed past the trusted fast lane so CORS headers are emitted. (#12900)

Consensus correctness (state-affecting fixes)

  • Zero-value balance credits no longer create an empty/dead account under EIP-158/EIP-161. (#13520)
  • Zero-nibble extension nodes are rejected in proofs — a canonical trie never emits one, and other clients forbid it. (#13519)
  • EIP-8037 beacon-root updates use canonical system calls rather than ordinary capped-transaction gas initialization. (#13483)
  • Preserve the RIPEMD touch across nested reverts (go-ethereum parity). (#13016)
  • Reject deposit logs with non-canonical ABI offsets (stricter EIP-6110 validation; honest blocks unaffected). (#12895)
  • Detect Geth genesis format independent of property order. (#12784)

Txpool

  • Blob transactions persisted by a 1.39.x node are decoded correctly when a reorg re-adds them. The blob-pool storage format gained a cell-mask trailer in 2.0.0; reading a block's worth of older records back could mis-frame them and abandon the transaction-pool update for that block. Upgrading in place needs no action. (#13614)
  • Corrupt light-blob records are skipped on pool restore instead of aborting it; blob persistence after revalidation is atomic. (#13032, #13045)
  • Rlp/TxDecoder type-initializer cycle broken. (#13158)

L2 & other chains

  • Optimism: OP Superchain chain registry refreshed (~40 chainspecs); OP payload decoding hardened against a malicious offset table; protocol-version signaling fix. (#12963, #12920, #12805)
  • XDC: runs the patricia state backend so GetNodeData can still be served to Go XDPoSChain peers; epoch resolution below the fast-sync pivot, archive start at the XDPoS v2 switch, blacklisted-address pool rejection, rewards read as XDC amounts, and several reliability fixes. (#13478, #12974, #12917, #12879, #12852, #12872, #12878)

fix(core): create the generated jwt secret and node key readable by the owner only (#14552)

When Nethermind generates the Engine API JWT secret (`jwt.hex`) or a plain node key (`node.key.plain`), the file was created with the process umask, usually `0644`, so any local user on the machine could read it. Both files are now created with mode `0600` (owner read/write) on Linux/macOS, the same mode geth uses for its generated JWT secret and the repository already uses in `TdxService`. The mode is set when the file is created, so there is no moment where the file exists with the wider mode.

- `JwtAuthentication.FromFile` writes a generated secret through a `FileStream` with `UnixCreateMode = UserRead | UserWrite` on non-Windows systems.
- `NodeKeyManager` writes a newly generated `node.key.plain` through `IFileSystem.FileStream.New(path, FileStreamOptions)` with the same `UnixCreateMode`, instead of `WriteAllBytes` followed by a mode change.
- Both get their `FileStreamOptions` from one shared helper, `OwnerOnlyFile.CreateWriteOptions()` in `Nethermind.Core`.
- Not covered: files that already exist keep their current mode (Nethermind only reads them), and an existing empty `jwt.hex` that gets regenerated keeps its mode, because `UnixCreateMode` only applies when a file is created.

description:
Release v1.21.0 (2026-10-14)

CLI

  • Support pipeline IDs in pipelines history. (#6995)
  • Show a hint for previewing more rows in pipelines show. (#6995)
  • databricks environments setup-local now uses the environment in UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT when it is set, as uv sync does. (#7026)
  • databricks environments setup-local now supports uv workspace members: it uses the shared .venv at the workspace root and writes the dependency constraints to the root pyproject.toml. (#7018)

AI Runtime

  • Limit databricks air run submission preflight validation to one five-second attempt before continuing when the service is unavailable. (#6994)

Bundles

  • Bundle file uploads now use the multipart POST /api/2.0/workspace/import endpoint instead of the deprecated POST /api/2.0/workspace-files/import-file, raising the per-workspace upload rate limit and improving deploy throughput under concurrency. (#6149)
  • Diagnostic paths now quote map keys that are not identifiers, e.g. resources.jobs['${var.env}_job']. (#6980)
  • No longer include CLAUDE.md in the bundle templates, now that Claude supports AGENTS.md. (#7000)
  • Fix bundle deployment bind silently binding over a deployment state it could not read, which could take over a resource that was already managed by the bundle. (#6331)
  • databricks bundle deploy, databricks bundle sync and databricks sync now retry file, library, state and metadata uploads that fail with a transient server error (5xx or 408), instead of failing. (#7014)
  • databricks bundle deploy, databricks bundle sync and databricks sync now retry the workspace path check (workspace/get-status) when it fails with a transient server error (5xx or 408) or an HTTP/2 REFUSED_STREAM, instead of failing. (#7044)
  • Fixed experimental.immutable_folder failing validation for targets with mode: development ("file_path must start with '~/' or contain the current username"). (#7027)
  • Fixed experimental.immutable_folder failing with experimental.deployment_history ("workspace_info.file_path must be an absolute workspace path") and failing bundle validate when top-level permissions are set. (#7001)
  • Translate relative .env file paths in a job's environment_variables[].spec.files to their deployed workspace locations. (#6985)
  • Resolve job project_environment paths relative to the YAML file that defines them. (#6983)

Dependency Updates

  • Bump Go toolchain to 1.26.9. (#6996)
  • Update Go SDK to 0.188.0. (#7038)

build(deps): bump urllib3 from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0 in /python (#6915)

Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.


Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's
releases.




2.8.0


🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support


urllib3
is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure
long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or
organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in
Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing
financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and
maintained for the long-haul.


Thank you for your support.


Security


Fixed the following security issues:


    

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or
overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
    • 

  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked()
could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High
severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
    • 

  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium
severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)
    • 





[!IMPORTANT]
urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or
overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that
behavior may require changes.


Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in
proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with
proxy_assert_hostname or
proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates
and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy
connections.






[!NOTE]
CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of
release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.




Deprecations & Removals


    

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry
option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)
    • 



Features


    

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and
Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the
result of parse_url(). (#4945)
    • 

  • Added basic_auth_encoding and
proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to
urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)
    • 



Bugfixes


    

  • 

    Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header
lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112,
preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as
Set-Cookie. (#1362)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with
ProxyManager when
use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing
ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for
HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a
FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)
    

    • 

  • 

    Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool
initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the
queue module after the ConnectionPool is
instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls
class property. This is done because sometimes the
queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such
as by gevent. (#3289)
    

    • 

  • 

    Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of
ValueError when retrying a request whose body had
tell() but not seek(). (#3779)
    

    • 

  • 

    Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating
with the proxy server. (#3785)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread
response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt
when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms
accepted by socket.connect, such as hex
(0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal
integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate
verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading
FullPoolError instead of ValueError when
called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created
with block=True. (#5059)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values
instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool
selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and
HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071,
#5101)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the
assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint
parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy
forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before
sending requests. (#5079)
    

    • 

  • 

    Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential
security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and
HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and
Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on
newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the
same security fixes. (#5091)
    

    •

ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy
identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when
forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and
continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an
HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters,
malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in
HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel
targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization
rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved
characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained
percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

description:
[SSH] Check port_fwd_serverless_enabled before starting serverless compute (#7063)

## Changes

A serverless `databricks ssh connect` (CPU or `--accelerator`) now reads
the `port_fwd_serverless_enabled` workspace setting first, in
ProxyCommand mode too. When an administrator has turned it off, connect
stops before it creates the secret scope, uploads binaries or submits
the server run:

```
Connecting to my-session...
Error: port forwarding to serverless compute is disabled for this workspace (setting port_fwd_serverless_enabled), and the SSH tunnel needs it. Ask a workspace or account admin to enable it, or connect to a dedicated cluster with --cluster
```

- `checkPortForwardingToServerless` reads the setting with
`WorkspaceSettingsV2.GetPublicWorkspaceSetting` and refuses only when
the read succeeds and `effective_boolean_val` is `false`.
- A read that fails is logged at debug level and connect continues. The
driver proxy's 403 from #7057 then stops it.
- `libs/testserver` answers the settings GET, defaulting
`port_fwd_serverless_enabled` to `true` like the real setting.

## Why

Stacked on #7057, PR 2 of DECO-28889. #7057 makes connect stop on the
driver proxy's 403, but by then it has uploaded binaries and started
serverless compute. The setting is what the proxy enforces, so checking
it first avoids both.

The CLI can't see everything the proxy's gate
(`PortForwardingToServerlessGate`) checks. The gate also needs its
enforcement flag on and skips allow-listed ports, and the setting is
only served through the public API in dev and staging
(`public_api_stage: STAGING`; production answers `Setting
port_fwd_serverless_enabled is not enabled for public API`). So a failed
read is never an error, and the 403 handling stays as the backstop. The
acceptance test for that backstop now stubs the settings read the way
production answers it.

## Tests

- Unit: `TestCheckPortForwardingToServerless` covers disabled, enabled,
no effective value, and a failed read. Plus new
`libs/testserver/settings_test.go` tests.
- Acceptance: new
`acceptance/ssh/connect-serverless-port-forwarding-disabled` checks the
error and that connect sent no requests besides reads.
`connect-serverless-feature-disabled` keeps covering the 403 path, with
the settings read failing. All `acceptance/ssh` tests pass.
- Manual, dogfood, setting off: serverless CPU, `--accelerator
GPU_1xA10`, and ProxyCommand mode (`ssh -o ProxyCommand="databricks ssh
connect --proxy --name …"`) all stop within 1 s with the error above.
- Manual, dogfood, setting on: serverless connects and runs the remote
command.

Enable errorlint for error comparisons and type assertions (#7084)

## Changes
Enable `errorlint` with only its comparison and type-assertion checks,
and fix its 29 findings: `err == ErrX` becomes `errors.Is(err, ErrX)`
and `err.(*T)` becomes `errors.AsType[*T](err)`. The `errorf` check
(`%v` → `%w` in `fmt.Errorf`) stays off: wrapping makes the cause
visible to every `errors.Is`/`errors.As` up the stack (e.g.
`fs.ErrNotExist`, `context.Canceled`), so converting its 36 sites is a
behavior change that needs per-site review in a separate PR.

## Why
These checks break silently as soon as the error is wrapped with `%w`.
No current site is broken, since every sentinel is still returned
unwrapped, but the codebase was inconsistent: for example
`cmd/bundle/validate.go` compared `root.ErrAlreadyPrinted` with `!=`
while `cmd/bundle/utils/process.go` uses `errors.Is`.

## Tests
golangci-lint reports 0 issues on the root and tools modules. Unit tests
pass for every changed package, and the `cmd/` and `bundle/validate/`
acceptance tests pass. One test keeps its `!=` with a
`//nolint:errorlint`, because it checks that `mapUploadError` returns
the same error rather than a wrapper.

description:
Remove auth workspace picker limit and support ID search (#7071)

## Why

`databricks auth login` against an account host lists the account's
workspaces and asks you to pick one. Accounts with more than 50
workspaces only saw the first 50, so the workspace you needed could be
missing, and the only way out was rerunning with `--workspace-id`.
Search also only matched names, so knowing the ID didn't help.

Fixes [BR-2184](https://databricks.atlassian.net/browse/BR-2184),
including the picker used by `ug configure`.

## Changes

Before: the picker showed the first 50 workspaces and only searched by
name.
Now: the picker includes every workspace and you can search by name or
ID.

- Removed the 50-workspace cap in `promptForWorkspaceSelection`. The SDK
list call has no pagination or search parameters, so it's still one
request and filtering stays local.
- Added `newWorkspaceSearcher`, which matches case-insensitive name
substrings and ID substrings. An exact ID match narrows the list to that
workspace, so typing `123` doesn't also show `1234`.
- Every row shows the workspace ID, the highlighted row gets the same
`▸` marker as the profile picker, and workspaces without a name render
as their ID. The label now says `(search by name or ID)`.
- Skip and the manual ID prompt (used when listing fails) behave as
before.
- Exported `termtest.Run` so command-level prompts can use the same
terminal harness as the `cmdio` prompt tests.

## Test plan

- [x] Searcher unit tests: name, ID, exact-ID precedence, whitespace,
duplicate names, empty names, non-ASCII names, Skip.
- [x] Picker tests through the real SDK list/decode path against a local
server: more than 50 workspaces, no-results recovery, list errors,
non-interactive mode, plus a golden snapshot of the rendered list.
- [x] `./task checks`, `./task lint-q`, `./task fmt-q`, and the
`cmd/auth/login` acceptance tests.
- [x] Synthetic 1k/10k/100k workspace lists through the SDK and terminal
picker: search p95 about 17 ms per keystroke. Startup at 100k is
dominated by fetching and decoding the full list, which the capped
version also did.
- [ ] Live account smoke test, including `ug configure`.

description:
bundle: read remote state files in one request instead of two (#7075)

## Changes
`stateFiler.Read` no longer calls `/api/2.0/workspace/get-status` before
`/api/2.0/workspace/export`. A 404 from export is mapped to
`fs.ErrNotExist`, which state pull already treats as "no state yet".

## Why
Every remote read of `resources.json`, `terraform.tfstate` and
`deployment.json` cost two sequential round trips. With deployment
history this sits on the critical path: the `resources.json` read
decides whether the CLI looks up `resources.deployment.json` and calls
GetDeployment.

The stat was never needed for state files; it came along with the code
it was copied from:
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/449 added it to the generic
workspace filer's `Read` when that switched to `/workspace/export`,
because non-direct export returns a directory as a DBC archive instead
of failing. It also replaced the explicit 404 mapping.
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/514 moved that filer to direct
download and kept the stat. The same week,
https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/515 removed the equivalent stat
from the DBFS filer and relied on SDK errors instead
(https://github.com/databricks/cli/issues/450). The workspace filer was
never revisited.
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/2423 introduced `stateFiler` to
read state over `GET /workspace-files` (no 10 MB cap) and copied the
stat and directory guard as-is, with no stated reason.
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6219 moved it to
`/workspace/export?direct_download=true` for scoped tokens. The stat
stayed; review focused on headers and goldens.

A directory at a state path is not a state file; its export now fails
with `parsing state` instead of `not a file`. `retry.Filer` only retries
overwrite writes (https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7014), so the
stat was never retried and no retry coverage is lost.

## Tests
Acceptance goldens updated. `resources/jobs/request-summary` (from
https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7077) shows the full per-command
request list: every `get-status` before a state file is gone; for files
that do not exist yet, a 404 `export` replaces it. Other goldens
(`user_agent`, `state`) change the same way. Not yet checked on a real
workspace: export's response for a missing path and for a directory.

cmdio: type-erase iterators in RenderIterator (#7072)

## Changes
`RenderIterator[T]` wraps the iterator as `listing.Iterator[any]` and
passes it to a non-generic renderer, so the pager and iterator renderers
compile once instead of once per SDK list type (~170 shapes, 2240
functions).

The type parameter was not used for anything type-specific: every
renderer converted the element to `any` right after `Next`
(`json.MarshalIndent`, `[]any` buffers for `template.Execute` and the
pager). The conversion now happens once in `anyIterator[T].Next`, so
output is unchanged.

## Why
Binary size: the stripped linux/amd64 release build goes from 55.8 MB to
52.5 MB (-3.3 MB).

## Tests
Existing cmdio unit tests and acceptance tests for workspace/account
commands.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

Co-authored-by: Isaac

[SSH] Fail fast when the driver proxy refuses the tunnel (#7057)

## Changes

`databricks ssh connect` now stops at the first 403 from the driver
proxy and prints the proxy's own message, instead of polling `/metadata`
until the 5-minute server start timeout. It also cancels the run it
submitted, since no client can ever reach that server.

```
Starting SSH server...
Job submitted successfully with run ID: 1035981371775948
Error: failed to ensure that ssh server is running: the workspace refused the SSH tunnel connection: FEATURE_DISABLED: An administrator has disabled port forwarding to serverless compute for this workspace, which includes the SSH tunnel used by `databricks ssh connect`
```

- `getServerMetadata` turns a 403 into the new
`errDriverProxyForbidden`, carrying the response body with its JSON
quotes removed. It isn't joined with `errServerMetadata`, so the first
call (the reuse path) returns it as is instead of submitting a new
server.
- The wait loop returns that error immediately and cancels its own run,
best effort (`cancelSSHServerRun`). A server found running on the reuse
path is never cancelled.
- Every other non-200 is still retried, for example `400 INVALID_STATE`
from a `metadata.json` that points at a terminated cluster.
- `libs/testserver` gains a settings v2 PATCH handler, and its fake
driver proxy returns the real `FEATURE_DISABLED` body while
`port_fwd_serverless_enabled` is `false`.

## Why

When an administrator turns off `port_fwd_serverless_enabled`, the
driver proxy answers every request to the tunnel server with `403` and
the body `"FEATURE_DISABLED: …"` (a JSON string, not the usual error
object). The client counted any non-200 as "server not up yet", so the
user watched "Waiting for the SSH server to start..." for 5 minutes and
then got `server is not ok, status code 403`, while the serverless
compute stayed up.

This is PR 1 of DECO-28889. PR 2 adds a check of
`port_fwd_serverless_enabled` before any compute is started, with this
403 handling as the fallback when the setting can't be read. PR 3 adds
telemetry error categories for both.

## Tests

- Unit: `TestMetadataResponseError` covers a 403 with the real body, a
non-JSON body and an empty body, plus a 400 and a 502 that are still
retried.
- Acceptance: new `acceptance/ssh/connect-serverless-feature-disabled`
turns the setting off through the API, then checks the error and the
recorded `runs/cancel`. It finishes in 1.6 s, so connect gives up on the
first 403. All other `acceptance/ssh` tests still pass.
- Manual, dogfood (setting off): serverless CPU failed after 31 s with
the message above, most of it uploading binaries. Run `1035981371775948`
ended `TERMINATED / CANCELED`.
- Manual, dogfood: a dedicated cluster (`0907-190337-c3qelmbu`) still
connects and runs the remote command.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

Bump Go to 1.27.2 and golangci-lint to v2.14.0 (#7052)

## Changes
Bump Go to 1.27.2 (`go 1.27.0`) in all modules and golangci-lint to
v2.14.0. v2.12 can't read Go 1.27 export data.

Lint config:
- `exhaustruct` → `exhaustruct_v5`, gofumpt `extra-rules` →
`extra.group-params` (both deprecated upstream).
- recvcheck v0.3 now excludes `Unmarshal*` by default instead of
`Marshal*`, which turned every value-receiver `MarshalJSON` into a
finding (37). Re-added the `Marshal*` exclusions.
- Removed linters that other linters now cover: `intrange` (modernize
`rangeint`), revive `context-keys-type` (SA1029), `waitgroup-by-value`
(govet copylocks), `range-val-in-closure` (no-op since Go 1.22),
ruleguard `rule_reflect_typefor` (modernize `reflecttypefor`),
`rule_os_chdir` (usetesting). I checked each one against a probe file.

Fixes from the new lint output: modernize `embedlit` (Go 1.27
field-selector keys, e.g. `resources.Job{Tasks: ...}` instead of
`resources.Job{JobSettings: jobs.JobSettings{Tasks: ...}}`),
`strings.CutLast`, gofumpt 0.12 formatting, two printf bugs found by the
new vet check (`%d` with `*int64`, `%w` with a pointer error), `wg.Go`,
and `nolint` on deprecated SDK fields that staticcheck 0.8 now flags in
composite literals. Also dropped a manual body drain in
`libs/auth/introspect.go`, because Go 1.27 drains HTTP/1 bodies on
`Close`.

## Why
Stay on a supported Go version. Two user-visible effects:
- `encoding/json` now runs on the v2 implementation, and syntax errors
point at a different position. For `{"a": 1,}` the old error was `1:9:
invalid character '}' looking for beginning of object key string`, the
new one is `1:8: invalid character ',' looking for beginning of value`.
Updated 3 unit tests and the `cmd/api/request-handling` golden.
`GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` would restore the old behavior, but I didn't use
it.
- Go 1.27 binaries require macOS 13 or later.

## Tests
`./task checks`, golangci-lint (root + tools), all unit tests, and the
full acceptance suite pass locally.

description:
[Release] Release v1.21.0

## Release v1.21.0

### CLI

 * Support pipeline IDs in `pipelines history`. ([#6995](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6995))
 * Show a hint for previewing more rows in `pipelines show`. ([#6995](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6995))
 * `databricks environments setup-local` now uses the environment in `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` when it is set, as `uv sync` does. ([#7026](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7026))
 * `databricks environments setup-local` now supports uv workspace members: it uses the shared `.venv` at the workspace root and writes the dependency constraints to the root `pyproject.toml`. ([#7018](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7018))

### AI Runtime

 * Limit `databricks air run` submission preflight validation to one five-second attempt before continuing when the service is unavailable. ([#6994](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6994))

### Bundles

 * Bundle file uploads now use the multipart `POST /api/2.0/workspace/import` endpoint instead of the deprecated `POST /api/2.0/workspace-files/import-file`, raising the per-workspace upload rate limit and improving deploy throughput under concurrency. ([#6149](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6149))
 * Diagnostic paths now quote map keys that are not identifiers, e.g. `resources.jobs['${var.env}_job']`. ([#6980](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6980))
 * No longer include `CLAUDE.md` in the bundle templates, now that Claude supports `AGENTS.md`. ([#7000](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7000))
 * Fix `bundle deployment bind` silently binding over a deployment state it could not read, which could take over a resource that was already managed by the bundle. ([#6331](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6331))
 * `databricks bundle deploy`, `databricks bundle sync` and `databricks sync` now retry file, library, state and metadata uploads that fail with a transient server error (5xx or 408), instead of failing. ([#7014](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7014))
 * `databricks bundle deploy`, `databricks bundle sync` and `databricks sync` now retry the workspace path check (`workspace/get-status`) when it fails with a transient server error (5xx or 408) or an HTTP/2 `REFUSED_STREAM`, instead of failing. ([#7044](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7044))
 * Fixed `experimental.immutable_folder` failing validation for targets with `mode: development` ("file_path must start with '~/' or contain the current username"). ([#7027](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7027))
 * Fixed `experimental.immutable_folder` failing with `experimental.deployment_history` ("workspace_info.file_path must be an absolute workspace path") and failing `bundle validate` when top-level `permissions` are set. ([#7001](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7001))
 * Translate relative `.env` file paths in a job's `environment_variables[].spec.files` to their deployed workspace locations. ([#6985](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6985))
 * Resolve job `project_environment` paths relative to the YAML file that defines them. ([#6983](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6983))

### Dependency Updates

 * Bump Go toolchain to 1.26.9. ([#6996](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6996))
 * Update Go SDK to 0.188.0. ([#7038](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/7038))

description:
Retry workspace get-status on transient failures during sync (#7044)

## Changes
`EnsureRemotePathIsUsable` validates the sync target with a
`workspace/get-status` read. Its calls now go through `libs/retry`
(added in #7014) with a new `retry.IsTransientRead` predicate: on top of
the 5xx/408 errors `IsTransient` already covers, an idempotent read is
also safe to replay after a transport-level failure that produced no
HTTP response (a `*url.Error`, e.g. the HTTP/2 `REFUSED_STREAM` in
#6472). `IsTransient` (used for the write path) is left unchanged.

## Why
#6472: a sporadic HTTP/2 `REFUSED_STREAM` on the `get-status` call
during `bundle deploy` aborted the deploy and left the bundle out of
sync with its artifacts. #7014 added upload retries; this extends the
same approach to the get-status read that was the actual point of
failure.

## Tests
- Unit test for `IsTransientRead` (5xx/408, a `REFUSED_STREAM`
`*url.Error`, and the non-retriable cases).
- Acceptance test (`cmd/sync/get-status-504`) injecting a 504 on `GET
/api/2.0/workspace/get-status` during `databricks sync`; the read is
retried and the sync succeeds. The transport-error branch is unit-tested
rather than acceptance-tested: the HTTP testserver can't produce a real
stream error, and Go's transport auto-retries idempotent GETs on reused
connections, which makes a forced-disconnect fault non-deterministic to
assert.

Builds on #7014 (now merged).

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.
