description:
dbt-core 1.13.0-b1 - October 14, 2026

Breaking Changes

  • Flags introduced in 1.9 and 1.10 defaults to true (#12713)

Features

  • Make MAXIMUM_SEED_SIZE_MIB configurable (#7117, #7124)
  • Bundle the dbt-state plugin (>=2.18,<3.0) as an install dependency of dbt-core. The plugin is opt-in: PluginManager skips auto-discovery unless the user passes --manage-state on the CLI, sets DBT_ENGINE_MANAGE_STATE=true, or sets manage_state to true in the flags block of dbt_project.yml (equivalently in the config block of profiles.yml). Discovery filters disabled modules before importlib.import_module is called, so the default opt-in-off state incurs no import cost. (#13014)
  • Add --use-v2-parser to delegate parsing to the fusion parser, load its manifest.json into a runtime Manifest, and bypass dbt-core's parser. Configurable via --v2-parser / DBT_ENGINE_V2_PARSER (defaults to dbt-core-experimental-parser parse) or the flags: section of dbt_project.yml. (#13029)
  • Add support for user settings with flags reading writing (#13031)
  • Add dbt login command (#13032)
  • Tolerate dbt Fusion-specific warn_error_options names instead of erroring, emitting a note that they are ignored because they are specific to the dbt Fusion engine (#12885)
  • Emit anonymous usage telemetry when state management is enabled via the --manage-state flag, DBT_ENGINE_MANAGE_STATE env var, or manage_state project config, including which surface supplied the opt-in (#15222)
  • Add catalog_database field to CatalogWriteIntegrationConfig (v1) so catalogs.yml can set a database-name override for any catalog type; works in conjunction with the dbt-adapters get_catalog_database_override method to give catalog_database highest priority in generate_database_name (#15156)
  • Add OpenTelemetry span instrumentation for node and hook execution, gated behind the --snowflake-projects-otel flag (off by default) (#11367)
  • Add hints for cli users based on dbt usage (#15510)
  • Warn users if they are using a deprecated dbt version (#15964)
  • Add otel_trace_id() and otel_span_id() Jinja functions to correlate query comments and model SQL with OpenTelemetry trace/span ids (#)
  • Announce dbt v2 availability as an INFO message on dbt --version, with a link to the v2 install docs (#)

Fixes

  • Reconstruct unrendered config kwarg values as readable expressions instead of raw AST repr (#15336)
  • Fix partial parsing raising a duplicate-metric CompilationError after a v2 inline model entry (semantic_model: true) is modified. Non-simple metrics (cumulative, derived, ratio, conversion) stored in schema_file.metrics were not cleaned up by _delete_v2_semantic_model_for_model, leaving stale unique_ids that triggered a false duplicate on the next parse. (#13004)
  • Fix deferred function references to use alias instead of bare name (#12895)
  • Cap the Python recursion limit while resolving the selector: method so a circular selector dependency raises a clean DbtRecursionError instead of crashing the process. The previous code relied on Python's default recursion limit (1000) tripping before the OS thread stack overflowed, but on platforms with smaller default stacks (notably Windows, ~1 MB vs ~8 MB on Linux/macOS) the margin can disappear once instrumentation (e.g. coverage) or stack-heavy plugins join the call chain. Lower the limit locally (restored in finally) so the catchable RecursionError fires first on every platform. (#13014)
  • Honor --manage-state when DBT_ENGINE_MANAGE_STATE is set to false. The bundled dbt-state plugin reads DBT_ENGINE_MANAGE_STATE directly in its initialize(), so a CLI override of an opt-out env var was previously dropped silently: PluginManager loaded the plugin but the plugin self-disabled on import. PluginManager now normalizes os.environ to the Click-resolved value before importing each bundled plugin, so all three opt-in surfaces (--manage-state CLI, DBT_ENGINE_MANAGE_STATE env var, manage_state in dbt_project.yml / profiles.yml) behave consistently end-to-end. (#13014)
  • Strip dbt-core-only DBT_ENGINE_* env vars (e.g. DBT_ENGINE_USE_V2_PARSER, DBT_ENGINE_V2_PARSER) from the v2-parser subprocess env, and expand ~ in --v2-parser paths. Fusion hard-errors on unknown DBT_ENGINE_* vars, so enabling the v2 parser via DBT_ENGINE_USE_V2_PARSER previously broke the handoff. Stripping is keyed off click-bound options, so future core-only DBT_ENGINE_* additions are handled automatically. Non-click vars (DBT_ENGINE_STATE_*, recorder, deps) pass through unchanged. (#13029)
  • Write manage_state user_settings in all platform login flows unless explicitly disabled (#13032)
  • Make sure that expires_at in oauth_sessions is int so that its rust interoperable (#13032)
  • Allow for setting of OSI documents directory as project config (#13088)
  • Support lowercase "osi" directory (#13087)
  • Add a direct_parents attribute to model nodes carrying the nearest public ancestors only, and emit it in dbt ls --output=json for models. Lineage consumers can now render DAG edges from direct_parents instead of depends_on.nodes, which carries the full transitive closure across plugin boundaries (still required for node selection and cycle detection). The new attribute is runtime-only and is stripped during manifest serialization, so the manifest.json contract is unchanged. (#)
  • Make the latest_version_pointer collision check quoting/case aware so an unquoted latest-version alias differing from the pointer name only by case is correctly detected on case-insensitive warehouses (#15210)
  • Recognize Databricks adapter config keys (query_tags, zorder, options, unique_tmp_table_suffix, skip_optimize) in jsonschema validation so they no longer raise spurious CustomKeyInConfigDeprecation warnings (dbt-databricks#1540, dbt-databricks#1302) (#N/A)
  • Fix intermittent "references a model that does not exist" parsing error when unit testing versioned models, caused by non-deterministic filesystem parse order (#11139)
  • Fix partial parsing ghost-duplicate that raised a false "found two data_tests" error by cleaning up disabled generic and singular test nodes on schema re-parse (#)
  • Update reuse relations hint text (#15510)
  • Fix macro namespace resolution so a dbt project named after a macro no longer crashes with 'MacroGenerator' during dispatch (#15556)
  • Persist hint_ts in dbt_home and gate rw on bare Except clause to be more defensive (#15510)
  • Fix dbt build node count ("X of Y") being inflated when unit tests are selected, by adding the unit test count to num_nodes exactly once instead of on every dequeue while run_count is still 0 (#11185)
  • Stop resolving a unit test's tested model eagerly at parse time; resolve it only in the single deterministic post-parse pass so resolution no longer depends on filesystem parse order at all (deeper fix for (#11139)
  • Re-parse adapter macros from the installed adapter package after loading a Fusion-generated manifest, ensuring the user's installed dbt- version is used instead of Fusion's compile-time bundled copy (#15527)
  • Fix OpenTelemetry hook spans: name them by hook and transaction phase, skip calls that run no hooks, and add node context and status. (#11367)
  • Re-parse the built-in generic tests (test_not_null, test_unique, test_accepted_values, test_relationships) after loading a Fusion-generated manifest, so they are not permanently evicted and left undefined at test-compile time (#15914)
  • Write target/manifest.json from the corrected in-memory manifest after loading a Fusion-generated manifest, so the on-disk artifact reflects the rediscovered adapter macros actually used for compilation instead of Fusion's raw bundled macros (#)
  • Send the x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob header and accept 201 Created when uploading artifacts to an Azure Blob Storage signed URL, so artifact ingestion no longer fails with 400 MissingRequiredHeader on Azure-hosted regions. Upload errors now include the storage provider's error code alongside the status code. (#N/A)
  • Capture and re-emit fusion parser subprocess output through dbt-core's event system instead of letting it pass through to raw stdout/stderr, re-leveling each line by its json-compat severity when available (#15672)
  • Validate that a resolved package installation path stays within the configured packages-install-path (#N/A)
  • Relay the v2 (Fusion) parser's log output via --log-format otel instead of json-compat, dropping span noise, keeping fusion's error/warning codes, and fixing a latent bug where a stray fusion stderr line could abort the run under --warn-error (#)
  • Fix Dimension to satisfy the metricflow-semantic-interfaces protocol and bump the metricflow floor to 0.213.0 (#, #)
  • Bare wildcard FQN selectors (e.g. -s "f_*") now match nested models regardless of subfolder depth (#)
  • Fix cumulative metrics with an input_metric and a top-level window field (v2 metric spec) incorrectly failing to parse with a legacy nested-type_params error (#N/A)
  • Fix compiled_code not persisted to manifest.json when using --use-v2-parser (#)
  • Include semantic_manifest.json in the artifact set uploaded by --upload-to-artifacts-ingest-api, matching other run artifacts (#N/A)
  • Validate that tarball package download locations stay within the dbt downloads directory (#)

Under the Hood

  • Allow-list additional DBT_ENGINE_STATE_* engine env vars (EMIT_REUSED_STATUS, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, AUTH_URL, TOKEN_URL, API_URL) (#13002)
  • sync JSON schemas from dbt-fusion (#N/A)
  • Add v2-parser telemetry — forward dbt-core's invocation_id and set DBT_INVOCATION_ENV=dbt-core-v2-parser on the parser subprocess so embedded telemetry correlates with the host invocation, and emit V2ParserStart/V2ParserEnd events around the handoff so pre-startup failures (missing binary, schema mismatch) are also captured. Bumps dbt-protos lower bound to 1.0.514 for the new event messages. (#13029)

description:
Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse support as a spark platform flavor

* Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse support as a spark platform flavor

Closes #15580

Adds Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse support as a **platform flavor of the `spark` adapter**, following the `platform_hint` precedent already used for AWS EMR. There is no new adapter type: Fabric targets are `type: spark` profiles carrying the Fabric workspace and lakehouse ids, which route to a platform-specialized module inside `SparkAuth`. Connection is over the [Fabric Livy API](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-engineering/api-livy-overview) with Microsoft Entra ID auth.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which added a separate `fabricspark` adapter type, after @hope-wat suggested verticalizing into the spark flavor instead. The result is a considerably smaller change (14 files rather than 33) and Fabric projects inherit the spark adapter's static analysis support. The separate-type version is preserved on [`fabricspark-adapter-separate-type`](https://github.com/arkin-nz/dbt-core/tree/fabricspark-adapter-separate-type) if that shape turns out to be preferred.

Companion driver PR (required for the connection to work): adbc-drivers/spark#78, which adds Fabric support to the Livy transport (Entra credentials, Fabric Livy protocol compatibility).

Field names follow Microsoft's v1 `dbt-fabricspark` adapter, so existing v1 profiles work unchanged:

```yaml
my_profile:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: spark
      workspaceid: 
      lakehouse: 
      lakehouseid: 
      schema: 
      authentication: CLI   # or SPN (+ tenant_id/client_id/client_secret),
                            # environment, managed_identity, default
      lakehouse_schemas: true   # opt-in for schema-enabled lakehouses
```

`method` defaults to `livy` and `host` to the Fabric API endpoint for these targets. `type: fabricspark` is accepted as an alias and rewritten to `type: spark` at profile load, so profiles written for the v1 adapter keep working.

Both Fabric lakehouse flavours are supported:

- **Classic** lakehouses keep Spark's 2-part naming (`schema` is the lakehouse name).
- **Schema-enabled** lakehouses (`lakehouse_schemas: true`) use 3-part `lakehouse.schema.table` naming, Unity-Catalog-style, with the lakehouse in dbt's database slot.

1. **Auth** (`dbt-auth`, `dbt-adbc`) — a platform-specialized `spark::fabric` module, reached when a spark profile carries the Fabric GUID fields. Credential kind names and parameters match the MSSQL driver's `fedauth` conventions: a service principal rides in the username as `@` with the client secret as the password. Follows the crate's borrowed-data conventions; no existing enums, accessors, or accepted input shapes modified; a regression test pins plain-Spark profiles to the original path.
2. **Profiles** (`dbt-schemas`, `dbt-loader`) — Fabric fields fold into `SparkDbConfig`, with `method`/`host` defaults and lakehouse-as-database for schema-enabled targets. `threads` is now honored for spark profiles (it was silently ignored). The `type: fabricspark` alias is rewritten at load.
3. **Metadata and relations** (`dbt-adapter`) — `list_relations` for Spark now uses `SHOW TABLE EXTENDED`, and `DESCRIBE`/catalog fqns include the database when set.
4. **Macros** (`dbt-spark` package) — database name resolution for 3-part naming, schema create/drop as no-ops on classic lakehouses (where the lakehouse is itself the namespace), `file_format` defaulting to delta on Fabric targets, and snapshot relations carrying the database through.

Both are independent of Fabric and are separated in the commits above:

- **`list_relations`** previously went through the Databricks path, which queries `system.information_schema`. That is a Unity Catalog feature, so it was silently broken on plain Spark. `SHOW TABLE EXTENDED` exists on every Spark backend.
- **Seed types**: the seed type conversion had no Spark arms, so seeds emitted PostgreSQL types (`text`, `float8`, `timestamp without time zone`) that Spark SQL rejects at `CREATE TABLE`. Spark now maps alongside Databricks (`string`, `bigint`, `double`, `timestamp`).

- **jaffle-shop: 28/28** (3 seeds, 5 models, 20 tests) on **both** classic and schema-enabled lakehouses, including through the `type: fabricspark` alias.
- Materializations verified: seeds, views, tables, incremental (append, merge with unique_key, `--full-refresh`), snapshots (timestamp strategy, SCD2 valid_from/valid_to).
- Idempotent re-runs; schema auto-creation on schema-enabled lakehouses.
- Auth via Azure CLI verified live. SPN, environment and managed identity are unit-tested; live coverage welcome in warehouse validation.
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` clean on all touched crates; unit tests added for fabric auth parsing, the profile alias, `SHOW TABLE EXTENDED` parsing, and Spark seed types.

- Python models are not supported (matches v1).
- Since these targets are `type: spark`, static analysis applies to them without any adapter-list change.
- Happy to restructure commits, rename things, or move to the separate-type shape, whatever suits the team. Also coordinating with the Microsoft `dbt-fabricspark` maintainer on v1/v2 parity.

This requires the companion driver change (adbc-drivers/spark#78) to be present in the Spark driver binary that dbt installs. As written, `SPARK_DRIVER_VERSION` still pins the current CDN release, so the correct landing order is:

1. Merge adbc-drivers/spark#78
2. Publish a new Spark driver build to the dbt CDN (dbt Labs)
3. Add the new version to the driver manifest/checksums and bump `SPARK_DRIVER_VERSION` (happy to push that commit here once the artifact exists)
4. Re-run adapter validation against the distributed binary

Until then this PR is intentionally stacked on #78, flagging explicitly so it isn't merged ahead of the driver release.

description:
fix(competitions): handle 404 errors during submission (#1216)

## Summary

While looking at the `kaggle competitions submit` flow, I found that the
404 handling condition was never reached for actual 404 responses.

The issue was with the `e.response` check. Since `requests.Response`
evaluates to `False` for error responses, the condition `if e.response
and e.response.status_code == 404` never matches a 404.

Because of this, users get a generic error hint that refers to an
owner/slug, which is not appropriate for competitions.

## Fix

I changed the condition to check `e.response is not None` so that 404
responses are handled correctly.

I also changed the handler to raise a `ValueError` instead of printing
the message and returning an empty string. This ensures the CLI reports
the error on stderr and exits with code `1`.

The error message now accounts for both file and code submissions, and
includes the server's error message for additional context.

Other HTTP errors and connection errors continue to propagate as before.
The Python library methods and the waiting/polling logic remain
unchanged.

## Tests

Added a new `TestCompetitionSubmitCli404` test class using real
`requests.Response` objects instead of `MagicMock`.

The tests cover:

- 404 responses during file and code submissions.
- Appropriate error messages for each submission path.
- Propagation of 500 responses and connection errors.
- CLI exit code and output streams when a 404 occurs.

The new 404 tests fail on the base branch and pass with this fix.

Ran `pytest tests/unit`: 1403 passed.

Also ran the Black formatting check, which passed. Mypy reports the same
11 pre-existing errors as the base branch, with no new errors.

This change is independent of the submission upload failure fix, and
both changes apply cleanly together.

Co-authored-by: stevemessick

fix(competitions): exit non-zero when submission upload fails (#1215)

## Summary

While looking at the `kaggle competitions submit` flow, I found that the
command exits with code `0` when the submission file upload fails.

The issue was that `competition_submit()` returns a response with an
upload failure message instead of raising an error. The CLI prints this
message but treats the command as successful, even though no submission
is created.

## Fix

I updated `competition_submit_cli` to raise a `ValueError` when the
upload fails. This uses the existing error handling in `main()`, so the
CLI now prints the error to stderr and exits with code `1`.

The Python library method `competition_submit()` remains unchanged to
preserve its existing behavior. The `--wait` and polling logic is also
untouched.

## Tests

Updated the existing test to check that an error is raised on upload
failure.

- Renamed `test_cli_skips_limits_on_upload_failure` to
`test_cli_raises_on_upload_failure`.
- Ran the submit, wait, and CLI tests: 105 passed.
- Ran the full unit test suite: 1398 passed.
- Ran the Black check using the project's pinned version, which passed.
- Tested the CLI with simulated HTTP 403 and 503 upload responses. Both
now exit with code `1` instead of `0`.

This change is limited to CLI error handling and does not modify the
Python library API or the waiting and polling flow.
product_or_resource: fix(competitions): exit non-zero when submission upload fails (#1215)

description:
What's Changed

Requires Python 3.10+. Python 3.9 reached end of life in October 2025, and the fixes for recent urllib3 security advisories require 3.10. On Python 3.9, pip will keep installing v2.8.0.

pip install --upgrade massive

New

  • Corporate networks: both clients now honor SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for TLS verification, or take a ca_certs= argument. RESTClient also takes a proxy= URL (WebSocket already uses HTTPS_PROXY). See the Network Configuration section of the README.
  • Faster multithreaded use: RESTClient keeps up to maxsize=10 connections open for reuse (previously 1), and other urllib3 pool options can be passed with connection_pool_kw.
  • Indices snapshots: IndicesSnapshot now includes last_updated and timeframe, and the new list_snapshot_indices returns all pages.
  • SEC filings: list_stocks_filings_8k_disclosures and list_stocks_taxonomies_disclosures (vX).

Fixes

  • *_any_of arguments given a comma-separated string (e.g. ticker_any_of="AAPL,VZ") were split into characters and returned the wrong data.
  • WebSocket server messages such as "Subscription limit reached", max_connections and slow_consumer are now logged as warnings instead of being silently dropped.
  • Dependency updates for security advisories in urllib3, requests, orjson and black.

Worth knowing when upgrading

  • If SSL_CERT_FILE or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is set, it's now used instead of the bundled certifi certificates, so make sure it points to a complete CA bundle. A variable pointing to a missing file is ignored with a warning.
  • WebSocket clients may log new WARNING lines on the WebSocketClient logger when the server reports a problem.

Thanks to @SachuJames, @Tyagiquamar, @jakobovski-arb, @romanzdk and @kevinchiu, whose PRs (#1034, #1033, #1026, #1008, #968) were combined into #1040.

All changes

  • Add proxy, custom CA, and connection pool options by @justinpolygon in #1040
  • Don't split comma-separated str values for *_any_of params by @justinpolygon in #1037
  • Log WebSocket server errors instead of dropping them by @justinpolygon in #1039
  • Add last_updated/timeframe to IndicesSnapshot and list_snapshot_indices by @justinpolygon in #1038
  • Require Python 3.10+ and update dependencies with security fixes by @dependabot in #1023
  • Bump idna from 3.7 to 3.15 by @dependabot in #1017
  • [bot] Add 8-K disclosures and disclosure categories endpoints by @justinpolygon in #1025
  • [PRO-1724] Add the skills plugin to the AI tools section of the README by @justinpolygon in #1036
  • [PRO-2007] Add AGENTS.md and AI tools section to README by @justinpolygon in #1035
  • [DEVREL-139] Update CODEOWNERS by @justinpolygon in #1024

Full Changelog: v2.8.0...v2.9.0

[SPT-1668] Add proxy, custom CA, and connection pool options (#1040)

Adds connection options to the clients, combining #968, #1008, #1026,
#1033 and #1034 (contributors are credited as co-authors).

- **Custom CA:** `ca_certs=` on `RESTClient` and `WebSocketClient`,
defaulting to `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, then certifi.
Closes #998.
- **Pool size:** `RESTClient(maxsize=10)`. urllib3 defaults to 1
connection per host.
- **Pool options:** `RESTClient(connection_pool_kw={...})`, merged over
the defaults. Closes #1009.
- **Proxy:** `RESTClient(proxy="http://user:pass@host:port")`. Proxy env
vars aren't read, so nobody's traffic changes route.

The README has a new **Network Configuration** section with examples for
each case (custom CA, proxy, threads, other pool options).

All new parameters are optional and added at the end of the signatures.
The one behavior change: if `SSL_CERT_FILE` or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`
points to a file, it's now used instead of certifi (as `requests` and
Python do). If it points to a file that doesn't exist, it's skipped with
a warning, so a stale value doesn't break anyone.

Verified against the live API through a local TLS-inspecting proxy
(mitmproxy with auth): REST and WebSocket connect with the proxy's CA
(argument or env var) and fail certificate verification without it;
wrong proxy credentials get 407. Under 16 threads, `maxsize=10` opened
16 TLS connections vs 57–70 with urllib3's default.

description:
[PRO-2007] Add AGENTS.md and AI tools section to README (#1035)

## Description

- Adds `AGENTS.md` with guidance for AI coding agents working on this
repo: commands, layout, conventions, and PR rules. This SDK is
hand-written, so AGENTS.md focuses on how to add a REST endpoint
(models, client methods, tests, docs).
- Adds an **AI tools** section to the README after the install step,
pointing to the hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.massive.com/`), the [AI
Tools quickstart](https://massive.com/docs/ai-tools/quickstart), and
[`llms.txt`](https://massive.com/docs/llms.txt). The same text goes into
all four SDK READMEs.
- Adds a one-line pointer to `AGENTS.md` in the README's Contributing
section.

## Related Issue

PRO-2007 (AGENTS.md) and PRO-2059 (AI tools section in the SDK READMEs).

## Motivation and Context

Developers using an SDK with Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT had no way to
learn from the README about the MCP server or llms.txt. Coding agents
working inside the repo also had no guidance. The skills plugin link is
left out until the public skills repo is live.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Documentation only, with no code changes. Checked that all the links
resolve. `mcp.massive.com` returns 401 without OAuth, which is expected.

description:
fix(app-server): draw streamed cells in the order of the final XML

Streaming adds every new cell at the end of its parent, and the merge
never moved existing cells, so a cell that first appeared in a later
partial was drawn over cells the final XML puts in front of it. The
edges of a Mermaid git graph, which drawio-mermaid places behind the
commits and their labels as Mermaid draws them, ended up on top of
both. After a routing or layout pass the XML behind Copy, Download and
Open in draw.io is serialized from the streamed graph, so it had the
wrong order too.

finalizeStreamingView now moves the cells into the order of the final
XML, under each parent (orderCellsAsInXml). Replaying the git graph of
the gallery line by line through the streaming merge in Chrome with the
viewer and drawio-mermaid bundles: before, the first edge came after
nine vertices and edges were drawn over commits; after, the model order
equals the XML order and every edge is behind the commits and labels.

Add a --baseline-ref option (Makefile BASELINE_REF=) to
compare_api_breakage.py so the public-API breakage check can diff the
current tree against a git ref (e.g. master or a merge-base) instead of
only a published PyPI release. The ref's wheel is built in a throwaway
detached worktree so poetry-dynamic-versioning stamps the ref's own
version, then cached under the workdir by commit SHA for fast reuse
across fix-and-recheck iterations. It is mutually exclusive with
--against.

Clean the cached worktree quietly (rmtree + `git worktree prune`) instead
of a blind `git worktree remove`, which errored loudly ("is not a working
tree") on first run. Also print phase banners (environment prep, wheel
builds, extraction, diffing) in non-verbose mode so long subprocess steps
no longer look hung.

Document BASELINE_REF in CONTRIBUTING.md (quickstart, flag table, and an
"Iterating against a git ref" section) and cover the new _build_ref_wheel
helper with unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 

* Update CONTRIBUTING.md

Co-authored-by: Spenser Jones 

* fix(tools): keep baseline worktree cleanup local to this run

Repo-wide git worktree prune drops unrelated missing worktrees. Reclaim only this path with add --force, and baseline the docs against origin/master so a stale local master is not reported as this branch's API breakage.

description:
Changed

  • 数字员工回复复用 chat — 通用发送与引用回复增加 stdin 正文、投递回执和绑定上下文校验；本地数字员工 worker 使用通用 chat 回传，保留已发布的 channel reply / channel operator-private 兼容入口，新宿主改用通用 chat，配套 DSH 要求 chatDelivery=true，缺失时提示升级；双方须配套升级。
  • A2UI 审批卡片兼容 — 发卡命令支持 --summary 自定义聊天预览，满足 DSH 数字员工的卡片能力探测；省略时继续使用原有默认摘要。

local_agent 私聊权限读取 DEAP 已发布可见范围（成员及部门子树）；群聊以已入群为准，不叠加个人可见范围或本地群白名单，并修复空白名单漏订阅群内 @ 消息；群聊仅原生 @ 当前员工才触发，普通消息不进入模型。DSH 按 groupMembershipAccess 能力传递群上下文；其他场景保留本地白名单。DWS/DSH 共用绑定查询判定，固定管理 Profile，查询失败不回退放行。

Fixed

  • 数字员工本地 Agent 状态反馈 (#1475) — 在原消息上显示排队、思考、已完成、失败或待核查状态；执行失败时发送明确提示，正常结束但无回复文字时仅贴“收到”，并将表情更新与正文投递分开记录，避免提前显示完成或因表情失败重复执行。

  • 数字员工引用上下文 (#1475) — 本地 Agent 接收引用回复时同时获得被引用的消息内容，避免只能看到当前问题；保留普通输入、会话指令及原有授权范围。

  • 数字员工 Codex 本地任务 (#1475) — 修复内置 Codex 误用群聊机器人的附件问答限制，允许按用户请求和现有权限使用本地技能与 CLI，保留沙箱配置，并避免会话恢复失败后静默新建、丢失上下文。

  • 数字员工图片输入 (#1475) — 自动下载直发或引用图片并交给本地 Agent，Codex 使用原生图片输入，避免只有 mediaId 无法识别；下载失败明确提示并保留失败状态。

  • 数字员工回执查询 — 等待发送回执时，对 im/query_message_send_status 返回的结构化错误码 1001 重查原发送任务，兼容回执尚未落库的短暂窗口；查询和等待共享最多 2 秒预算，到期报告送达状态未知，不重新发送消息。

  • 数字员工自身消息识别 — connect 使用员工自己的登录身份精确解析自身开放 ID，避免发布详情与入站事件的身份作用域不同而产生自回复。旧配置没有员工 Profile 作用域标记时，原生 worker 和 DSH 启动阶段只解析自身一次；失败拒绝启动，不依赖主管、不逐消息查询、不修改原绑定、模型、权限或会话。

  • 数字员工平台入站权限 — 正式绑定的 local_agent 直接使用平台保证的私聊投递和群内 @ 权限，不再逐消息查询可见范围、通讯录或部门；其他本地通道保持白名单。旧绑定缺少主管 Profile 也可正常启动，删除仅用于可见范围的主管迁移和启动阻断。新绑定不再写入该历史字段，固定 operator 审批、绑定版本与解绑检查保留。DSH 通过 bindingAccessPolicy 能力读取明确访问策略，需配套新版插件。

  • Windows 图片与卡片契约 — Markdown 本地图片识别盘符路径及标准 file URI；内嵌 A2UI 解释资源在检出时保持 LF，避免摘要因换行转换失配。修正数字员工工作目录、附件及导出路径的跨平台测试夹具。

  • 升级下载 — 官方开源版独立安装继续通过 npm 查询版本，改为只下载同版本 GitHub Release 的当前平台归档和技能包，避免下载包含其他平台的完整 npm 包。官方 Release 查询优先使用环境变量或本机 GitHub CLI 已有凭据，无可用凭据时匿名查询；凭据不进入 Registry 或资产下载。强制验证资产大小、SHA256 和二进制版本；失败时不自动回退全包。--dry-run 展示预计下载量，--skip-skills 省去技能包下载。自定义源和包管理器升级保持原有行为。

Added

  • 本地图文混排 — chat message send --content 和 chat +messages-send --as user --markdown 自动上传行内本地图片，保留前后文字；支持预览、内容去重及最多三路并发上传。

  • 图文图片上传 — 使用上传返回的 mediaIdV2 构建图文消息；缺少 V2 时终止发送，避免使用不符合图片下载接口契约的编号。个人收藏表情保留原有媒体编号选择行为。

  • 图文图片编号复用 — 发送时识别裸 V2 图片编号；读取 Markdown 和富文本图片后生成带消息、会话身份的下载参数。

  • 图文图片错误提示 — 使用固定诊断区分文件读取、路径校验和上传失败，保留敏感路径保护，并提供对应的处理建议。

  • 新增全局隐藏参数 --delegator-user-id、--delegator-corp-id 和 --delegator-open-dingtalk-id。根命令在本次执行作用域持有校验后的不可变身份快照，公共 runner 统一向四个内置 HTTPS MCP 网关透传；旧 helper 丢弃 context 时也能补入身份，无需按业务逐条改造。无效输入整组省略；旧文档委托入口保持兼容，新旧协议禁止混用。实际委托授权依赖网关和业务服务接入。

  • 修复 AI 表格主服务、辅助服务、分页、重试、视图更新和工作流发布的上下文传递，保留取消信号；扩展真实命令到 HTTP Header 的回归矩阵，并覆盖串行 root 复用和多个预建 root 的身份隔离。同进程多 root 并发执行不在支持范围，并发调用使用独立 CLI 进程。

  • 更新 DWS 业务接入指南：说明公共 runner 覆盖条件、真实命令测试和绕行通道的接入要求；插件、stdio、发现、scoped 换票、独立 published MCP、直接 OpenAPI、文件字节传输及事件长连接继续排除，跨源重定向清理和 UID 发送边界保持不变。

Fixed

  • 媒体下载提示 — dws chat message download-media 的 Help 说明返回的下载地址临时有效，提示使用原 mediaId 及消息、会话信息重新下载。

本版本将已交付的 v1.0.64-beta.1 晋级正式版，汇总该 beta 的变化，并纳入下方列出的 beta 后变更。

Added

  • Pi Coding Agent 接入 — 新增 --channel pi，支持官方 JSON 流式文本、模型覆盖、按会话隔离和重启续聊；ask 模式禁用工具。
  • 通讯录好友与事件 — 增加好友列表、申请列表、发送和处理申请、删除好友，以及好友申请和添加事件；统一使用 openDingTalkId，提供到 userId 的查询入口，补齐昵称、备注、状态和 Agent 使用说明。写操作要求明确确认，删除好友属于高风险操作。
  • OpenHarmony 发布包 — 增加静态自签名的 openharmony/arm64 归档和 SHA256，集成 SafeChat 消息加密；npm 与 Homebrew 的平台范围保持原有配置。
  • 版本检查与升级提示 — auth status、version 和 --version 提供限时、可缓存、可关闭的更新检查；未知输入优先给出具体纠错建议，仅在缺少明确建议时检查新版，保留原错误类别、退出码和机器输出。

Changed

  • AI 表格契约与公开同步 — 精确登记 24 项幂等性声明纠正，并限定已审查的公开同步补丁；未登记接口及风险、确认要求和执行效果的兼容保护继续生效。

Fixed

  • AI 表格写入、等待与筛选 — 保留原始 clientToken，未知写入停止重放并通过只读对账恢复；补齐批次分组与旧回执兼容。建表、建字段提供有时限的结构核对，超时或取消不重复创建；统一查询、批量更新的筛选校验及 Help、Schema、Skill 说明。
  • 日历、白板与 AI 卡片 — 修复日历嵌套时区与忙闲字段的写后核验，读回失败时保留写入回执；白板在预览或远端调用前校验 OpenNodes 层级与文本样式。更新 AI 卡片协议索引、兼容预检、预览及业务标识处理，补齐白板和卡片使用说明。
  • 升级来源与安装方式 — 开源版默认通过 npm Registry 查询版本；包管理器安装交由对应工具升级，独立二进制校验 npm 包完整性与资产 SHA256 后自更新，无需 npm 或 Node.js。保留备份、回滚和 Skill 更新，修复 npm 强制升级、同版本重装及安装文档中的环境变量传递。

Changes since v1.0.64-beta.1

Removed

  • Chat Thread — 下线 chat thread promote，历史调用返回 command_retired，帮助与 Skill 不再推荐该命令。已有消息转为话题暂无等价替代；新建话题使用 chat thread send，回复已有话题使用 chat thread reply。

  • 招聘产品下线 — 开源版移除 dws recruit job list、get、create 及整个招聘产品域的内置注册、Schema、MCP 端点和 Skill 入口。招聘能力仅在千问办公专属版维护。

Fixed

  • wget-only install of the latest release (#1456) — resolving latest without curl now requests the GitHub releases URL directly, so wget can read the release tag instead of failing before the download.

  • 修正 npm 包的问题反馈、仓库和主页链接，统一指向 DingTalk-Real-AI/dingtalk-workspace-cli，避免 npm bugs 打开 404 页面。

  • 招聘退役兼容检查 — 精确登记已批准的开源招聘产品退役，避免仍含招聘能力的旧稳定版阻塞后续 PR 和发布兼容检查；其他产品和接口的兼容保护保持生效。

* fix: fail when no given message id exists

store_flags returns how many of the given messages were found, on
every backend. flag add, set and remove, message move and copy, and
message delete when it moves to the trash fail when that is zero, and
the flag commands report the count.

Over IMAP, where UID STORE, COPY and MOVE answer OK for UIDs matching
nothing, the count comes from the STORE echoes or the COPYUID, and
from a UID SEARCH on the same set for what they leave unsaid.

The plain output of the flag commands and of message delete ends with
a newline.

description:
Upgrade notes

  • Gmail drafts can now be deleted, and the delete is permanent. If you already set AGENT_EMAIL_DELETE_ENABLED=true, delete_email on Gmail now permanently deletes drafts (Gmail has no trash for drafts) without AGENT_EMAIL_HARD_DELETE_ENABLED. Callers must still pass user_explicitly_requested_deletion: true. Sent and received Gmail mail still can't be deleted and returns NOT_SUPPORTED. Leave AGENT_EMAIL_DELETE_ENABLED unset if agents should not delete drafts.
  • delete_email returns provider failures instead of throwing, on every provider including Microsoft 365. Check for { success: false, error: { code, message } }. A missing Gmail message returns MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Other provider failures return DELETE_FAILED or the provider's own code. description:
fix(smtp): quote the HTML original as escaped text, not raw markup

Automated review of the reply-quoting commit found two real gaps:

- quoteOriginalAsHtml embedded original.bodyHtml directly inside the
  
. That body is sender-controlled; an unbalanced tag
  (a stray 
) could break out of the quote boundary and
  have the rest render as if it were the reply's own content rather
  than quoted material. Now always goes through stripHtml first and
  wraps the escaped result in 
, same as the plain-text fallback
  already did — trading the original's own HTML formatting for that
  guarantee.

- oneLine()'s line-break collapse only matched \r and \n. NEL
  (U+0085), LINE SEPARATOR (U+2028) and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (U+2029)
  are line breaks to some renderers but not to that regex, so a
  sender using one of those in a display name could still forge a
  second attribution line — exactly what oneLine existed to prevent.
  The same gap let a body line using one of them slip past the "> "
  quote prefix in quoteOriginalAsText. Both now normalize the full
  set first.
product_or_resource: fix(smtp): quote the HTML original as escaped text, not raw markup

description:
feat(skills): add the deploy-slack-app skill for Railway and Heroku (#153)

* feat(deploy): add the deploy-slack-app skill for Railway and Heroku

Gives developers a path from an app that works locally to one that keeps
running after the local process stops, using the Slack CLI deploy hook so
the skill never handles a token itself.

The hook script is provider-agnostic and sources a small per-target file,
so adding a provider is one reference file rather than a change to the
script. Railway and Heroku ship; both run the app in Socket Mode.

Adds four tool-selection eval scenarios, two that should route to the new
skill and two that pin the boundaries against slack-cli and slack-docs.

* fix(deploy): require the deploy flags and Heroku team ownership found in real runs

A real end-to-end Railway deploy surfaced a prompt Step 5 did not cover.
'slack deploy' asks which app to target, and in a non-interactive shell that
prompt is fatal: the CLI reports that the input device is not a TTY and nothing
deploys. '--team' and '--app deployed' answer it, and '--app deployed' is the one
most easily missed because the prompt only appears on a project that has never
been deployed.

A real Heroku run surfaced two more. Salesforce-managed accounts cannot own a
personal app, so 'apps:create' needs '--team'; the target script now takes
HEROKU_TEAM. And 'apps:info' reports the same 'Couldn't find that app' for an app
that does not exist and one owned by a stranger, because Heroku app names are
globally unique, so a generic name fails later at create time instead.

* fix(deploy): scale the stray Heroku web dyno to zero and correct the cost claim

A real Heroku deploy ran two copies of the app. The Node buildpack contributes a
default 'web' process type even though the Procfile declares only 'worker', and
Heroku starts it on the first release. That second copy opened its own Socket Mode
connection, so Slack reported "num_connections": 2 and delivered events to
whichever copy it picked, and it never booted successfully either, because a Socket
Mode app binds no port and Heroku kills a web dyno that does not bind $PORT within
60 seconds. It sat in a restart loop, opening a fresh connection every cycle, and
billed as a second dyno. The worker's own logs looked healthy throughout, so
nothing about this was visible from the place a developer would look.
'target_deploy' now scales worker up and web down in one call.

The same run disproved the cost line. A team app cannot use the Eco plan and gets
Basic dynos billed per dyno, so the '$5/month' figure only holds for a personal
app. Salesforce-managed accounts cannot own a personal app at all, which makes the
team case the default rather than the exception for anyone in that position.

* refactor(deploy-slack-app): one self-contained script per provider

Replace the orchestrator + four-function contract with one linear,
self-contained deploy script per provider, on disk, syntax-highlighted.
The agent no longer extracts bash out of a fenced markdown block.

- Delete references/deploy.sh and its target_* seam.
- Add references/heroku/deploy.sh and references/railway/deploy.sh
  as real executable files.
- Reduce references/heroku.md and references/railway.md to prose:
  cost, caveats, install, project prereqs, env vars, re-deploy,
  verifying.
- Collapse SKILL.md Step 4 from three sub-steps to two.

Behaviour is unchanged. The Railway path was re-verified end to end
on macOS against a fresh bolt-js-starter-template scaffold.

Windows support becomes additive: two .ps1 files beside the two .sh
files, no orchestrator to port twice.

* refactor(deploy-slack-app): install the deploy script as .slack/deploy-.sh

Keep the deploy script out of the project root and name it after the
provider, so it sits beside hooks.json and says which host it targets.
The hook now points at ./.slack/deploy-railway.sh or
./.slack/deploy-heroku.sh.

- Rename references/railway/deploy.sh and references/heroku/deploy.sh
  to references/deploy-railway.sh and references/deploy-heroku.sh, so
  each source file shares its installed name.
- Update SKILL.md Step 4 for the new paths, and ask before changing an
  existing deploy key that points at a different script.
- Note in each script that the CLI runs the hook from the project root,
  so its relative paths still resolve there.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): point to live pricing instead of quoting plans

The skill is installed on developer machines and can outlive a provider's
price list, so a quoted plan or trial term can go stale without us
shipping an update. Replace prices, plan names, and trial terms with
links to each provider's pricing page, and tell the agent to read or
link those pages rather than quote from memory.

- Keep the lasting reasons to pick a provider: secrets on stdin, deploy
  from the working directory vs from git, and personal vs team billing.
- Replace the Render and Fly.io comparison with the two checks that
  apply to any provider: an always-on worker process type, and how it
  is billed.
- Generalise the Heroku idle-sleep check so it no longer names a plan
  or a timeout.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): wrap pricing URLs in angle brackets for lint

* docs(deploy-slack-app): note macOS and Linux scope in the changeset

* docs(deploy-slack-app): describe the deployed app as a separate Slack app

The deploy creates a second Slack app with its own app ID in .slack/apps.json. The old wording read as if the local development app kept running on the host.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): link pricing pages instead of fetching them

Fetching and summarising two pricing pages spends the developer's tokens on every deploy. The skill now hands over the links and keeps only the cost facts that do not change with the price list.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): describe team-only Heroku accounts without naming a company

* docs(deploy-slack-app): drop Railway comparison from the Heroku token note

An agent reads this after the developer has already chosen Heroku, so the Railway aside invites a mid-deploy provider switch or a --stdin flag Heroku does not have. Step 2 already makes the comparison where the choice happens.

* fix(deploy-slack-app): harden both deploy scripts for non-interactive agent runs

Railway: wait for the build with --ci instead of --detach, pass --workspace when set, bound every logs command with --lines, and name RAILWAY_API_TOKEN for headless auth.

Heroku: scale web=0 only when a web process type exists (the Python buildpack adds none), restart instead of an empty commit on an up-to-date push, reuse the app named by the heroku git remote, require a committed Procfile and at least one commit, and verify config without printing the tokens.

Skill: add a Prepare the Provider step, show how provider variables reach the hook, keep the language-specific get-hooks value, cover Bolt for Python and remote manifests, and drop repeated notes.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): note Railway workspace lookup and re-deploy overlap

Found in a live Railway run: the skill said to ask when an account has several workspaces without saying how to check, and a re-deploy briefly shows num_connections 2 while Railway removes the old deployment.

* fix(deploy-slack-app): catch nested git repos and document Heroku first-deploy gaps

Found in live Heroku runs with Bolt for JavaScript and Bolt for Python. slack create does not run git init, so a project inside another repository passed the git checks and would have pushed the parent's code. The deploy script now stops in that case.

The docs now say to commit .slack/apps.json after the first deploy, to add a .python-version for Bolt for Python, and that num_connections 2 is expected while the first release's web dyno shuts down.

* docs(deploy-slack-app): route Request URL and Windows requests to the skill

The description no longer says "Socket Mode only, on macOS and Linux", which
told agents to skip the skill for those developers before they could see why
the case is unsupported. The Request URL and Windows stop messages now ask the
developer to update the plugin, since support may have shipped, and link
#172 and #171 to upvote. Two routing evals pin both cases.

* feat(deploy-slack-app): add a teardown step for Railway and Heroku

Step 8 deletes the provider's copy and the deployed Slack app after one
confirmation, and leaves the development app in place. Verified end to end
on both providers: `railway unlink` needs `--yes`, `heroku apps:destroy`
removes the git remote itself, and `slack app delete --force` removes
`.slack/apps.json`. Railway schedules the project's removal, so the
reference explains why it stays listed. Adds a routing eval for teardown.

* fix(deploy-slack-app): ask which team to deploy into when there is more than one

The agent reused the team from .slack/apps.dev.json, often a developer
sandbox, instead of asking. That can install the app into a team the
developer did not intend, and a later deploy to the right team creates a
second Slack app. Step 2 now asks for the team as well as the provider.

---------

Co-authored-by: William Bergamin
